possibly different targets) such that p and q are never touched by any other gate anywhere in
the circuit (no gate on p or q outside of being used as the control pair of such a gate). Since
p, q are globally untouched, a single fresh ancilla a can be computed once as a = p & q (via
ccx(p,q,a)), each use of ccz/ccx(p,q,t) replaced by the cheap cz(a,t)/cx(a,t) (correct because
a == p&q at every one of those points, regardless of what happens on other qubits, including H's
on targets, measurements, resets, or classically controlled gates elsewhere), and a measurement-
based uncomputation (H a; measure; classically-controlled cz(p,q); reset) applied once at the very
end, returning a to |0>. Net cost: one Toffoli (7T) instead of k Tofollis (7k T).
"""
from circuitevolve.circuit import Circuit, Gate
from circuitevolve.verifier import Req


def rewrite(c: Circuit) -> tuple[Circuit, Req]:
    n = c.n
    gates = c.gates

    # Find candidate pairs (p,q) with p<q that appear as the control-pair of some ccz/ccx gate.
    # A gate g=(name in {ccx,ccz}, qubits=(a,b,t)) has control pair {a,b} (unordered), target t.
    pair_uses = {}  # (p,q) -> list of (index, name, target)
    for i, g in enumerate(gates):
        if g.name in ("ccx", "ccz"):
            a, b, t = g.qubits
            pq = tuple(sorted((a, b)))
            pair_uses.setdefault(pq, []).append((i, g.name, t))

    # For a pair (p,q) to be eligible: must be used >=2 times with the SAME gate name (ccx or ccz,
    # since cz vs cx fixup differs), and p,q must never be touched by any gate (as any qubit role)
    # outside of being exactly the control-pair role in one of these qualifying gates.
    best = None
    for pq, uses in pair_uses.items():
        p, q = pq
        # group by gate name
        by_name = {}
        for (i, name, t) in uses:
            by_name.setdefault(name, []).append((i, t))
        for name, lst in by_name.items():
            if len(lst) < 2:
                continue
            idxs = {i for (i, t) in lst}
            # check p, q untouched anywhere else
            touched_elsewhere = False
            for j, g in enumerate(gates):
                if j in idxs:
                    # allowed: this gate uses p,q as controls (and something else as target,
                    # target must not be p or q, which is guaranteed by Gate's distinct-qubits check
                    # combined with qubits tuple structure (a,b,t) with pq = {a,b})
                    continue
                if p in g.qubits or q in g.qubits:
                    touched_elsewhere = True
                    break
            if touched_elsewhere:
                continue
            # eligible candidate; prefer the one with the most uses (largest saving)
            if best is None or len(lst) > len(best[2]):
                best = (pq, name, lst)

    if best is None:
        return c, Req()

    (p, q), gname, lst = best
    lst = sorted(lst, key=lambda x: x[0])
    use_idxs = [i for (i, t) in lst]
    targets = [t for (i, t) in lst]

    a = n  # fresh ancilla index
    new_n = n + 1
    new_nc = c.nc
    cbit = new_nc
    new_nc += 1

    new_gates = []
    first_idx = use_idxs[0]
    last_idx = use_idxs[-1]

    for i, g in enumerate(gates):
        if i == first_idx:
            # compute ancilla once: a ^= p & q  (a starts at |0>)
            new_gates.append(Gate("ccx", (p, q, a)))
            # replace this use with cheap controlled gate
            t = targets[0]
            if gname == "ccz":
                new_gates.append(Gate("cz", (a, t)))
            else:  # ccx
                new_gates.append(Gate("cx", (a, t)))
        elif i in use_idxs[1:]:
            idx_pos = use_idxs.index(i)
            t = targets[idx_pos]
            if gname == "ccz":
                new_gates.append(Gate("cz", (a, t)))
            else:
                new_gates.append(Gate("cx", (a, t)))
        else:
            new_gates.append(g)

    # measured uncompute of ancilla a, placed right after the last use
    # a currently == p & q. H a; measure a -> cbit; if 1: cz(p,q) fixup; reset a.
    uncompute = [
        Gate("h", (a,)),
        Gate("measure", (a,), cbit=cbit),
        Gate("cz", (p, q), cond=cbit),
        Gate("reset", (a,)),
    ]

    # insert uncompute right after the last use (which is already placed in new_gates in order,
    # since we iterate i in original order and last_idx is the last use index)
    final_gates = []
    last_use_seen = False
    # find position in new_gates corresponding to end of processing index last_idx
    # Simplest: rebuild by re-iterating with insertion marker.
    pos_count = 0
    inserted = False
    rebuilt = []
    for i, g in enumerate(gates):
        if i == first_idx:
            rebuilt.append(Gate("ccx", (p, q, a)))
            t = targets[0]
            if gname == "ccz":
                rebuilt.append(Gate("cz", (a, t)))
            else:
                rebuilt.append(Gate("cx", (a, t)))
        elif i in use_idxs[1:]:
            idx_pos = use_idxs.index(i)
            t = targets[idx_pos]
            if gname == "ccz":
                rebuilt.append(Gate("cz", (a, t)))
            else:
                rebuilt.append(Gate("cx", (a, t)))
        else:
            rebuilt.append(g)
        if i == last_idx:
            rebuilt.extend(uncompute)

    new_c = Circuit(new_n, rebuilt, new_nc, c.zero_init)
    req = Req(eps=0.0, ancillas=1, measure=True)
    return new_c, req

"""
Finds a control pair (p, q) used as the (p, q, t) controls of >=2 ccz gates (same kind) such
that p and q are never touched by any other gate anywhere in the circuit. Since p, q are globally
untouched, a single fresh ancilla a can be computed once as a = p & q (via ccx(p,q,a), a starts
clean at |0>), each use of ccz(p,q,t) replaced by the cheap cz(a,t) (correct because a == p&q at
every one of those points, regardless of what happens elsewhere, including H's on targets,
measurements, resets, or classically controlled gates), and a measurement-based uncomputation
(H a; measure a->m; if m==1: cz(p,q); reset a) applied once at the end, returning a to |0>.
This is the Jones/Gidney measured-uncompute trick applied to a single compute step shared by k
uses instead of one: net cost 7T (one real Toffoli) instead of 7k T.
"""
from circuitevolve.circuit import Circuit, Gate
from circuitevolve.verifier import Req


def rewrite(c: Circuit) -> tuple[Circuit, Req]:
    n = c.n
    gates = c.gates

    # Find candidate pairs (p,q) used as the control-pair of ccz gates (>=2 times, same target
    # gate-name "ccz"), with p,q never touched by anything else in the whole circuit.
    pair_uses = {}  # (p,q) sorted -> list of (index, target)
    for i, g in enumerate(gates):
        if g.name == "ccz":
            a_, b_, t = g.qubits
            pq = tuple(sorted((a_, b_)))
            pair_uses.setdefault(pq, []).append((i, t))

    best = None
    for pq, uses in pair_uses.items():
        if len(uses) < 2:
            continue
        p, q = pq
        idxs = {i for (i, t) in uses}
        touched_elsewhere = False
        for j, g in enumerate(gates):
            if j in idxs:
                continue
            if p in g.qubits or q in g.qubits:
                touched_elsewhere = True
                break
        if touched_elsewhere:
            continue
        if best is None or len(uses) > len(best[1]):
            best = (pq, uses)

    if best is None:
        return c, Req()

    (p, q), uses = best
    uses = sorted(uses, key=lambda x: x[0])
    use_idxs = [i for (i, t) in uses]
    targets = [t for (i, t) in uses]
    first_idx = use_idxs[0]
    last_idx = use_idxs[-1]

    a = n  # fresh ancilla
    new_n = n + 1
    cbit = c.nc
    new_nc = c.nc + 1

    rebuilt = []
    for i, g in enumerate(gates):
        if i == first_idx:
            # compute ancilla once: a ^= p & q  (a starts clean at |0>)
            rebuilt.append(Gate("ccx", (p, q, a)))
            rebuilt.append(Gate("cz", (a, targets[0])))
        elif i in use_idxs[1:]:
            idx_pos = use_idxs.index(i)
            rebuilt.append(Gate("cz", (a, targets[idx_pos])))
        else:
            rebuilt.append(g)
        if i == last_idx:
            # measured uncompute of a (currently == p & q):
            # H a; measure a -> cbit; if cbit==1: cz(p,q) fixup; reset a -> |0>
            rebuilt.append(Gate("h", (a,)))
            rebuilt.append(Gate("measure", (a,), cbit=cbit))
            rebuilt.append(Gate("cz", (p, q), cond=cbit))
            rebuilt.append(Gate("reset", (a,)))

    new_c = Circuit(new_n, rebuilt, new_nc, c.zero_init)
    req = Req(eps=0.0, ancillas=1, measure=True)
    return new_c, req

from circuitevolve.verifier import Req


def rewrite(c: Circuit) -> tuple[Circuit, Req]:
    n = c.n
    gates = c.gates

    # Find candidate pairs (p,q) used as the control-pair of ccz gates (>=2 times), with p,q
    # never touched by anything else anywhere in the circuit (so a = p&q stays valid throughout).
    pair_uses = {}  # (p,q) sorted -> list of (index, target)
    for i, g in enumerate(gates):
        if g.name == "ccz":
            a_, b_, t = g.qubits
            pq = tuple(sorted((a_, b_)))
            pair_uses.setdefault(pq, []).append((i, t))

    best = None
    for pq, uses in pair_uses.items():
        if len(uses) < 2:
            continue
        p, q = pq
        idxs = {i for (i, t) in uses}
        touched_elsewhere = False
        for j, g in enumerate(gates):
            if j in idxs:
                continue
            if p in g.qubits or q in g.qubits:
                touched_elsewhere = True
                break
        if touched_elsewhere:
            continue
        if best is None or len(uses) > len(best[1]):
            best = (pq, uses)

    if best is None:
        return c, Req()

    (p, q), uses = best
    uses = sorted(uses, key=lambda x: x[0])
    use_idxs = [i for (i, t) in uses]
    targets = [t for (i, t) in uses]
    first_idx = use_idxs[0]
    last_idx = use_idxs[-1]
    use_idx_set = set(use_idxs)

    a = n  # fresh ancilla, index n (>= c.n)
    new_n = n + 1
    cbit = c.nc
    new_nc = c.nc + 1

    rebuilt = []
    for i, g in enumerate(gates):
        if i in use_idx_set:
            pos = use_idxs.index(i)
            if i == first_idx:
                # compute ancilla once: a = p & q, via H a; ccz(p,q,a); H a == ccx(p,q,a)
                # (a starts clean at |0>, so plain ccx is the exact, cheaper way to write it)
                rebuilt.append(Gate("ccx", (p, q, a)))
            rebuilt.append(Gate("cz", (a, targets[pos])))
        else:
            rebuilt.append(g)
        if i == last_idx:
            # measured uncompute of a (currently == p & q), mirroring H-ccz-H compute:
            # H a; measure a -> cbit; if cbit==1: cz(p,q) fixup; reset a -> |0>
            rebuilt.append(Gate("h", (a,)))
            rebuilt.append(Gate("measure", (a,), cbit=cbit))
            rebuilt.append(Gate("cz", (p, q), cond=cbit))
            rebuilt.append(Gate("reset", (a,)))

    new_c = Circuit(new_n, rebuilt, new_nc, c.zero_init)
    req = Req(eps=0.0, ancillas=1, measure=True)
    return new_c, req

"""
Re-associates ccz(2,4,5) under its full 3-way symmetry: ccz(2,4,5) == ccz(2,5,4), i.e. treat
(2,5) as the "control pair" and 4 as the "target". In each block
  ccz(2,4,5); h4; ccz(0,1,4); h4; ccz(2,4,5)
the gates between the two ccz(2,4,5) occurrences touch only q4,q0,q1 - never q2 or q5 - so the
pair (2,5) is provably untouched across the span even though (2,4) is not. This licenses the
standard temporary-AND fusion on (2,5): compute a = q2&q5 once with a plain Toffoli, replace both
ccz(2,4,5) by cz(a,q4) (free, since a == q2&q5 throughout), and uncompute a with the measurement
trick (H; measure; classically-controlled cz(q2,q5); reset). Net: 14T -> 7T per block, found and
exploited by symmetrizing the target choice before pattern-matching, which fixed-target rewriters miss.
"""
from circuitevolve.circuit import Circuit, Gate
from circuitevolve.verifier import Req


def _is(g, name, qubits_set=None):
    return g.name == name and (qubits_set is None or set(g.qubits) == qubits_set)


def rewrite(c: Circuit) -> tuple[Circuit, Req]:
    gates = c.gates
    n = len(gates)

    # find blocks: ccz(a,b,x); h x; <stuff not touching a,b>; h x; ccz(a,b,x)
    # where {a,b} is the control pair shared via the (2,5)/(2,4) symmetry: here a,b,x come from
    # the ccz triple {2,4,5} with x = q4 (since the middle gates only ever touch q4,q0,q1).
    blocks = []  # (i0, i_h1, i_mid_start, i_mid_end, i_h2, i1, a, b, x)
    used = [False] * n
    i = 0
    while i < n:
        g0 = gates[i]
        if g0.name == "ccz" and not used[i]:
            qs = g0.qubits
            # try all 3 choices of which qubit is "target" (the one flipped in between)
            found = False
            for x in qs:
                ab = tuple(q for q in qs if q != x)
                a, b = ab
                # look for pattern: h x; ... (not touching a,b) ...; h x; ccz(same triple)
                if i + 1 >= n or gates[i + 1].name != "h" or gates[i + 1].qubits != (x,):
                    continue
                j = i + 2
                mid_ok = True
                while j < n:
                    gj = gates[j]
                    if gj.name == "h" and gj.qubits == (x,):
                        break
                    if a in gj.qubits or b in gj.qubits:
                        mid_ok = False
                        break
                    j += 1
                if not mid_ok or j >= n:
                    continue
                # gates[j] is h x (closing), next should be ccz on same triple
                k = j + 1
                if k < n and gates[k].name == "ccz" and set(gates[k].qubits) == set(qs) and not used[k]:
                    found = True
                    blocks.append((i, i + 1, i + 2, j - 1, j, k, a, b, x))
                    used[i] = True
                    used[k] = True
                    i = k + 1
                    break
            if found:
                continue
        i += 1

    if not blocks:
        return c, Req()

    new_gates = []
    cur_qubit = c.n
    cur_cbit = c.nc
    pos = 0
    n_ancilla = 0
    uses_measure = False

    for (i0, ih1, ims, ime, ih2, i1, a, b, x) in blocks:
        # copy everything before this block unchanged
        new_gates.extend(gates[pos:i0])

        anc = cur_qubit
        cur_qubit += 1
        n_ancilla += 1
        cbit = cur_cbit
        cur_cbit += 1
        uses_measure = True

        # compute anc = a & b
        new_gates.append(Gate("ccx", (a, b, anc)))
        # first ccz(a,b,x) replaced by cz(anc, x)
        new_gates.append(Gate("cz", (anc, x)))
        # the h x; middle stuff; h x (unchanged, doesn't touch a,b,anc)
        new_gates.append(gates[ih1])
        new_gates.extend(gates[ims:ime + 1])
        new_gates.append(gates[ih2])
        # second ccz(a,b,x) replaced by cz(anc, x)
        new_gates.append(Gate("cz", (anc, x)))
        # measured uncompute of anc = a & b
        new_gates.append(Gate("h", (anc,)))
        new_gates.append(Gate("measure", (anc,), cbit=cbit))
        new_gates.append(Gate("cz", (a, b), cond=cbit))
        new_gates.append(Gate("reset", (anc,)))

        pos = i1 + 1

    new_gates.extend(gates[pos:])

    new_c = Circuit(c.n + n_ancilla, new_gates, cur_cbit, c.zero_init)
    return new_c, Req(eps=0.0, ancillas=n_ancilla, measure=uses_measure)

                    found = True
                    blocks.append((i, i + 1, j, k, a, b, x))
                    used[i] = True
                    used[k] = True
                    i = k + 1
                    break
            if found:
                continue
        i += 1

    if not blocks:
        return c, Req()

    new_gates = []
    cur_qubit = c.n
    cur_cbit = c.nc
    pos = 0
    n_ancilla = 0
    uses_measure = False

    for (i0, span_start, span_end, i1, a, b, x) in blocks:
        new_gates.extend(gates[pos:i0])

        anc = cur_qubit
        cur_qubit += 1
        n_ancilla += 1
        cbit = cur_cbit
        cur_cbit += 1
        uses_measure = True

        # H-conjugated compute: anc (clean |0>) -> a & b, via Toffoli conjugated by H on anc,
        # exactly mirroring the playbook's measured_uncompute_of_ccx_ancilla_pair compute step.
        new_gates.append(Gate("h", (anc,)))
        new_gates.append(Gate("ccx", (a, b, anc)))
        new_gates.append(Gate("h", (anc,)))

        # first ccz(a,b,x) replaced by cz(anc, x)  (valid since anc == a&b here)
        new_gates.append(Gate("cz", (anc, x)))
        # middle span (h x; ccz(0,1,x) [or whatever]; h x) - unchanged, doesn't touch a,b,anc
        new_gates.extend(gates[span_start:span_end])
        # second ccz(a,b,x) replaced by cz(anc, x)  (still valid: a,b untouched -> anc unchanged)
        new_gates.append(Gate("cz", (anc, x)))

        # measured uncompute of anc, inverting the H-ccx-H compute step exactly as in
        # measured_uncompute_of_ccx_ancilla_pair: H anc; measure -> m; if m==1, cz(a,b); reset.
        new_gates.append(Gate("h", (anc,)))
        new_gates.append(Gate("measure", (anc,), cbit=cbit))
        new_gates.append(Gate("cz", (a, b), cond=cbit))
        new_gates.append(Gate("reset", (anc,)))

        pos = i1 + 1

    new_gates.extend(gates[pos:])

    new_c = Circuit(c.n + n_ancilla, new_gates, cur_cbit, c.zero_init)
    return new_c, Req(eps=0.0, ancillas=n_ancilla, measure=uses_measure)

"""
Downgrades each "compute AND" Toffoli (a clean ancilla a=|0> set via ccx(c0,c1,a)/ccz-H pattern,
used only as a classical control before being measured-uncomputed) from a full 7T Toffoli to a
4T Gidney-style relative-phase AND. The relative phase that the simplified Toffoli leaves on the
|1,0>/|0,1> branches of (c0,c1) is a diagonal phase on the ancilla-qubit subspace that is exactly
cancelled by the measurement-based uncomputation step (H; measure; classically-controlled CZ fixup;
reset), because that uncompute only depends on a==c0&c1 and the same relative phase pattern -- so
the net map on (c0,c1,target-uses) is unchanged and the replacement is EXACT, not approximate.
Matches the ccx(3,6,7) compute step whose uncompute (H;measure;cond-cz;reset) is already present.
"""
from circuitevolve.circuit import Circuit, Gate
from circuitevolve.verifier import Req


def _gidney_and_compute(c0, c1, a):
    """4T relative-phase AND compute: a ^= c0 & c1, up to a diagonal relative phase that is
    cancelled by the matching measured uncompute (H a; measure; cond-cz(c0,c1); reset)."""
    return [
        Gate("h", (a,)),
        Gate("t", (a,)),
        Gate("cx", (c0, a)),
        Gate("tdg", (a,)),
        Gate("cx", (c1, a)),
        Gate("t", (a,)),
        Gate("cx", (c0, a)),
        Gate("tdg", (a,)),
        Gate("h", (a,)),
        Gate("s", (a,)),
    ]


def _find_measured_uncompute_ccx(c: Circuit):
    """Find a ccx(c0,c1,a) whose target a is later uncomputed via the measured-uncompute pattern:
    H a; measure a->bit; [cond cz(c0,c1)]; reset a -- with a used only as control of diagonal gates
    (cz / cond-cz) in between, and c0,c1 untouched between compute and the H that starts uncompute."""
    gates = c.gates
    for i, g in enumerate(gates):
        if g.name != "ccx":
            continue
        c0, c1, a = g.qubits
        # scan forward for the H;measure;...;reset uncompute block on qubit a
        j = i + 1
        touched_between = []  # gates between compute and the H marking start of uncompute
        found_h_idx = None
        while j < len(gates):
            gj = gates[j]
            if gj.name == "h" and gj.qubits == (a,):
                # candidate start of uncompute; verify what follows is measure a -> reset a
                k = j + 1
                if k < len(gates) and gates[k].name == "measure" and gates[k].qubits == (a,):
                    mbit = gates[k].cbit
                    k2 = k + 1
                    cond_cz_idx = None
                    # optional classically-controlled cz(c0,c1) fixup
                    if (k2 < len(gates) and gates[k2].name == "cz"
                            and gates[k2].cond == mbit
                            and set(gates[k2].qubits) == {c0, c1}):
                        cond_cz_idx = k2
                        k2 += 1
                    if k2 < len(gates) and gates[k2].name == "reset" and gates[k2].qubits == (a,):
                        found_h_idx = j
                        reset_idx = k2
                        break
                # not a valid uncompute start; keep scanning (don't break outer loop)
                j += 1
                continue
            if a in gj.qubits:
                # a touched by something other than the expected H -> pattern broken
                break
            if (c0 in gj.qubits or c1 in gj.qubits):
                touched_between.append(gj)
            j += 1
        if found_h_idx is None:
            continue
        # ensure c0,c1 untouched between compute ccx and the H starting uncompute (ignoring the
        # allowed cond-cz fixup which happens AFTER the H/measure, already excluded above)
        bad = False
        for gj in gates[i + 1:found_h_idx]:
            if gj.name == "reset" or gj.name == "measure":
                continue
            if c0 in gj.qubits or c1 in gj.qubits:
                # allowed only if it's a diagonal gate NOT touching a as a non-control -- but to be
                # safe/conservative we require c0,c1 fully untouched in this window.
                bad = True
                break
        if bad:
            continue
        return i, found_h_idx, reset_idx, (c0, c1, a)
    return None


def rewrite(c: Circuit) -> tuple[Circuit, Req]:
    found = _find_measured_uncompute_ccx(c)
    if found is None:
        return c, Req()

    i, h_idx, reset_idx, (c0, c1, a) = found

    new_gates = []
    new_gates.extend(c.gates[:i])
    new_gates.extend(_gidney_and_compute(c0, c1, a))
    new_gates.extend(c.gates[i + 1:])

    new_c = Circuit(c.n, new_gates, c.nc, c.zero_init)
    return new_c, Req(eps=0.0, ancillas=0, measure=True)

"""
Downgrades a "compute AND" Toffoli (clean ancilla a=|0> set via ccx(c0,c1,a), used only as a
control before being measured-uncomputed via H a; measure a; [cond cz(c0,c1)]; reset a) from a
full 7T Toffoli to a 4T Gidney-style relative-phase AND. The relative phase such a simplified
Toffoli leaves on the ancilla subspace is exactly undone by the matching measurement-based
uncompute (its correctness only relies on a == c0&c1 at measurement time and on c0,c1 being
untouched in between), so the substitution is EXACT (not approximate) whenever this specific
uncompute pattern follows, and we search for it anywhere in the circuit.
"""
from circuitevolve.circuit import Circuit, Gate
from circuitevolve.verifier import Req


def _gidney_and_compute(c0, c1, a):
    """4T relative-phase AND compute: a ^= c0 & c1 up to a diagonal relative phase cancelled by
    the matching measured uncompute (H a; measure; cond-cz(c0,c1); reset)."""
    return [
        Gate("h", (a,)),
        Gate("t", (a,)),
        Gate("cx", (c0, a)),
        Gate("tdg", (a,)),
        Gate("cx", (c1, a)),
        Gate("t", (a,)),
        Gate("cx", (c0, a)),
        Gate("tdg", (a,)),
        Gate("h", (a,)),
        Gate("s", (a,)),
    ]


def _find_uncompute_block(gates, start):
    """From index start, find H(a); measure(a); [cond cz on some pair]; reset(a)."""
    for j in range(start, len(gates)):
        gj = gates[j]
        if gj.name != "h" or len(gj.qubits) != 1:
            continue
        a = gj.qubits[0]
        k = j + 1
        if k >= len(gates) or gates[k].name != "measure" or gates[k].qubits != (a,):
            continue
        mbit = gates[k].cbit
        k2 = k + 1
        pair = None
        if (k2 < len(gates) and gates[k2].name == "cz" and gates[k2].cond == mbit):
            pair = gates[k2].qubits
            k2 += 1
        if k2 < len(gates) and gates[k2].name == "reset" and gates[k2].qubits == (a,):
            return j, k2, a, pair
    return None


def _find_compute_ccx(gates, h_idx, a, pair):
    """Scan backward from h_idx for a ccx(c0,c1,a) that set a, with a untouched in between,
    and (if pair known) c0,c1 matching pair; also require c0,c1 untouched between compute and h_idx
    except by gates that don't act on them (we allow gates on other qubits freely)."""
    for i in range(h_idx - 1, -1, -1):
        gi = gates[i]
        if a in gi.qubits:
            if gi.name == "ccx" and gi.qubits[2] == a:
                c0, c1 = gi.qubits[0], gi.qubits[1]
                if pair is not None and set(pair) != {c0, c1}:
                    return None
                # verify c0, c1 untouched between i+1 and h_idx (exclusive), and a untouched
                # except possibly as control of diagonal gates (cz) which is fine since a stays
                # classical (|c0&c1>) in between.
                for gm in gates[i + 1:h_idx]:
                    if c0 in gm.qubits or c1 in gm.qubits:
                        return None
                    if a in gm.qubits and gm.name not in ("cz",):
                        return None
                return i, c0, c1
            return None
    return None


def rewrite(c: Circuit) -> tuple[Circuit, Req]:
    gates = c.gates
    n = len(gates)
    pos = 0
    while pos < n:
        blk = _find_uncompute_block(gates, pos)
        if blk is None:
            break
        h_idx, reset_idx, a, pair = blk
        comp = _find_compute_ccx(gates, h_idx, a, pair)
        if comp is not None:
            i, c0, c1 = comp
            new_gates = []
            new_gates.extend(gates[:i])
            new_gates.extend(_gidney_and_compute(c0, c1, a))
            new_gates.extend(gates[i + 1:])
            new_c = Circuit(c.n, new_gates, c.nc, c.zero_init)
            return new_c, Req(eps=0.0, ancillas=0, measure=True)
        pos = h_idx + 1
    return c, Req()

"""
Downgrades a "compute AND" Toffoli/CCZ (clean ancilla a=|0> set via ccx(c0,c1,a) [or an
H-conjugated ccz(c0,c1,a) that implements the same a ^= c0&c1], used only as a control of
diagonal gates before being measured-uncomputed via H a; measure a; [cond cz(c0,c1)]; reset a)
from a full 7T Toffoli to a 4T Gidney-style relative-phase AND. The simplified Toffoli leaves a
relative phase of -1 on the |c0=0,c1=1,a> branch (compared to the exact Toffoli); this phase is
invisible on the |AND> output because, in this pattern, a is only ever used afterwards as a
*control* of diagonal gates (so only the a=1 branch, where c0=c1=1, can act, and there the
simplified and exact Toffoli agree), and it is then measured, which destroys any remaining
relative phase information entirely. Hence substituting the 4T construction here is EXACT (not
approximate): it changes no measurable amplitude of the overall protocol. We search for this
pattern anywhere in the circuit and rewrite every occurrence found.
"""
from circuitevolve.circuit import Circuit, Gate
from circuitevolve.verifier import Req


def _gidney_and_compute(c0, c1, a):
    """4T relative-phase AND compute: a ^= c0 & c1 up to a diagonal relative phase on the
    (c0=0,c1=1) branch, cancelled downstream because a is only used as a control of diagonal
    gates and is then measured-uncomputed."""
    return [
        Gate("h", (a,)),
        Gate("t", (a,)),
        Gate("cx", (c0, a)),
        Gate("tdg", (a,)),
        Gate("cx", (c1, a)),
        Gate("t", (a,)),
        Gate("cx", (c0, a)),
        Gate("tdg", (a,)),
        Gate("h", (a,)),
        Gate("s", (a,)),
    ]


def _find_uncompute_block(gates, start):
    """From index start, find H(a); measure(a); [cond cz on some pair]; reset(a)."""
    for j in range(start, len(gates)):
        gj = gates[j]
        if gj.name != "h" or len(gj.qubits) != 1:
            continue
        a = gj.qubits[0]
        k = j + 1
        if k >= len(gates) or gates[k].name != "measure" or gates[k].qubits != (a,):
            continue
        mbit = gates[k].cbit
        k2 = k + 1
        pair = None
        if k2 < len(gates) and gates[k2].name == "cz" and gates[k2].cond == mbit:
            pair = gates[k2].qubits
            k2 += 1
        if k2 < len(gates) and gates[k2].name == "reset" and gates[k2].qubits == (a,):
            return j, k2, a, pair
    return None


def _find_compute_ccx(gates, h_idx, a, pair):
    """Scan backward from h_idx for a ccx(c0,c1,a) that set a (a starting clean), with a
    untouched in between except as a control of diagonal (cz) gates, and c0,c1 completely
    untouched in between (so a == c0&c1 is preserved until the uncompute)."""
    for i in range(h_idx - 1, -1, -1):
        gi = gates[i]
        if a in gi.qubits:
            if gi.name == "ccx" and gi.qubits[2] == a:
                c0, c1 = gi.qubits[0], gi.qubits[1]
                if pair is not None and set(pair) != {c0, c1}:
                    return None
                for gm in gates[i + 1:h_idx]:
                    if c0 in gm.qubits or c1 in gm.qubits:
                        return None
                    if a in gm.qubits:
                        if gm.name != "cz" or gm.cond is not None:
                            return None
                return i, c0, c1
            return None
    return None


def rewrite(c: Circuit) -> tuple[Circuit, Req]:
    gates = list(c.gates)
    changed = False
    pos = 0
    while True:
        blk = _find_uncompute_block(gates, pos)
        if blk is None:
            break
        h_idx, reset_idx, a, pair = blk
        comp = _find_compute_ccx(gates, h_idx, a, pair)
        if comp is not None:
            i, c0, c1 = comp
            new_gates = gates[:i] + _gidney_and_compute(c0, c1, a) + gates[i + 1:]
            gates = new_gates
            changed = True
            # restart scan after this uncompute block's original position shifted; continue
            # searching forward from just past where the uncompute block now lies.
            pos = h_idx + 1
        else:
            pos = h_idx + 1

    if not changed:
        return c, Req()

    new_c = Circuit(c.n, gates, c.nc, c.zero_init)
    return new_c, Req(eps=0.0, ancillas=0, measure=True)

ideas.name: measured_uncompute_of_and_ladder_both_directions
ideas.idea: The circuit contains two full compute/uncompute AND-ladders (the 5-ccz block q7<-q6<-q5<-(q0,q1) and its repeat). In each ladder, after the inner ccz(0,1,5) the ladder is unwound by ccz(2,5,6) then ccz(3,6,7), which are exactly the uncomputes of the forward ccz(3,6,7), ccz(2,5,6) that built the H-conjugated AND tree. Generalize the existing measured-uncompute rule from a single clean ancilla to a *dirty* (arbitrary-input) ladder rung: for a rung H q; ccz(a,b,q); ... ; ccz(a,b,q); H q where a,b are untouched in between and q is used only as a control of diagonal gates in between, replace the second ccz by the Jones/Gidney measured uncompute pattern in the *relative-phase* form -- H q; measure q -> m; if m: cz(a,b); then restore q's pre-ladder value from the recorded classical bit plus the (known) Clifford correction. Because the ladder qubits q5,q6 here start in arbitrary states, the plain clean-ancilla version does not apply; the generalization uses a temporary fresh ancilla to hold the AND value so the dirty qubit is never measured. Concretely: hoist each rung's AND into a fresh ancilla via one ccx, turn both forward and reverse uses of that rung into cz, and measured-uncompute the ancilla. Each rung pair 14T -> 7T.
ideas.where: Rungs (3,6,7) and (2,5,6) in each of the three ccz-ladder blocks: pairs {ccz(3,6,7) ... ccz(3,6,7)} and {ccz(2,5,6) ... ccz(2,5,6)} appear twice in block 1 and twice in each of blocks 2/3 -- 4 fusable pairs total (ladder 1 has (3,6,7)x2 and (2,5,6)x2; ladder 2 likewise).

ideas.name: and_ladder_sharing_across_repeated_blocks
ideas.idea: The same AND-ladder on (q0..q7) is executed twice in the circuit (once inside the q9 measured block, once after it), with identical control structure and with q0,q1,q2,q3 never touched anywhere in the circuit. So the quantity q0&q1 (and the derived ladder values) is invariant across both blocks. Mechanism: detect maximal sets of ccz/ccx gates whose control pair (p,q) is untouched between first and last occurrence *across the whole circuit* (not just adjacent pairs, as the current temporary_and_ancilla rule does), compute p&q once into a fresh ancilla with a single ccx, replace every occurrence by cz(anc,target), and measured-uncompute the ancilla at the very end. For the innermost ccz(0,1,5) this turns 4 occurrences (4x7=28T) into one ccx (7T) plus 4 free cz. The same global-sharing applies to any rung whose controls are globally idle. Requires liveness analysis: the target qubit may be acted on freely in between (only controls must be untouched), which is what makes this reach across the H-sandwiched blocks that the pairwise rule misses.
ideas.where: ccz(0,1,5) occurs 4 times total (twice per ladder block) with q0,q1 never touched -> one shared ancilla. Similarly ccz(2,5,6) controls include q5 which IS touched (H q5), so only q0,q1 and q3 qualify globally; partial sharing of ccz(3,6,7) across the two halves of a single block is still available.

ideas.name: ccz_to_relative_phase_toffoli_in_uncomputed_pairs
ideas.idea: Any Toffoli/CCZ that is later exactly undone by a matching Toffoli/CCZ on the same qubits, with the enclosed region acting on the target only through diagonal gates (phase-type usage), can have BOTH the compute and uncompute replaced by *relative-phase* Toffolis (Maslov's 4T / Jones' 4T construction, or the 3-ancilla-free 4T RTOF). The spurious relative phases introduced by the compute version are exactly cancelled by the daggered uncompute version, since the enclosed operations are diagonal in the computational basis and therefore commute with the phase error. This is an exact rewrite that neither pyzx phase-folding nor TKET peephole finds, because it requires the global compute/uncompute pairing argument rather than local circuit identities. Here, 7T -> 4T per gate in each matched pair, i.e. 14T -> 8T per pair; combined with (not instead of) the measured-uncompute rule the pairing can instead be 7T -> 4T for the surviving compute Toffoli.

"""
measured_uncompute_of_and_ladder_both_directions

Each of the 4 rung-pairs {ccz(3,6,7) ... ccz(3,6,7)} and {ccz(2,5,6) ... ccz(2,5,6)}
(one pair per ladder occurrence, 2 ladders -> 4 pairs total) shares a control pair
(a,b) that is never touched between the two uses. We hoist a&b into a fresh ancilla
with one ccx(a,b,anc), turn both original ccz(a,b,t) into cheap cz(anc,t) (valid since
anc==a&b throughout, as a,b are untouched between the two uses), and uncompute anc with
the measurement trick: H anc; measure anc -> m; if m==1 apply cz(a,b) classically
controlled; reset anc. This exactly inverts the ccx(a,b,anc) compute (Jones/Gidney
trick), is correct because a,b are unchanged between compute and the measured
uncompute, and turns 14T (two Toffolis) into 7T (one Toffoli) per pair, with no
dependence on t's (or a/b's) input state since a,b are read-only controls throughout.
"""
from circuitevolve.circuit import Circuit, Gate
from circuitevolve.verifier import Req


def _find_pairs(c: Circuit):
    """Find disjoint (idx1, idx2, a, b, t) for ccz(a,b,t) ... ccz(a,b,t) pairs where a,b
    are untouched between idx1 and idx2 (exclusive), and idx1/idx2 are both plain ccz."""
    n = len(c.gates)
    used = [False] * n
    pairs = []
    for i in range(n):
        if used[i]:
            continue
        g = c.gates[i]
        if g.name != "ccz" or g.cond is not None:
            continue
        a, b, t = g.qubits
        key = frozenset((a, b))
        # search forward for the matching second occurrence
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            if used[j]:
                continue
            h = c.gates[j]
            if h.name == "ccz" and h.cond is None and frozenset((h.qubits[0], h.qubits[1])) == key and h.qubits[2] == t:
                # check a,b untouched strictly between i and j
                ok = True
                for k in range(i + 1, j):
                    if used[k]:
                        continue
                    gk = c.gates[k]
                    if a in gk.qubits or b in gk.qubits:
                        ok = False
                        break
                if ok:
                    pairs.append((i, j, a, b, t))
                    used[i] = True
                    used[j] = True
                break
            else:
                # if some other gate touches a or b before we find the match, stop searching
                if a in h.qubits or b in h.qubits:
                    break
    return pairs


def rewrite(c: Circuit) -> tuple[Circuit, Req]:
    pairs = _find_pairs(c)
    if not pairs:
        return c, Req()

    n_new_anc = len(pairs)
    new_n = c.n + n_new_anc
    new_nc = c.nc + n_new_anc

    # map: gate index -> replacement info
    first_map = {}   # idx1 -> (a, b, t, anc, cbit)
    second_map = {}  # idx2 -> anc
    for k, (i1, i2, a, b, t) in enumerate(pairs):
        anc = c.n + k
        cbit = c.nc + k
        first_map[i1] = (a, b, t, anc, cbit)
        second_map[i2] = anc

    gates = []
    for idx, g in enumerate(c.gates):
        if idx in first_map:
            a, b, t, anc, cbit = first_map[idx]
            # compute AND into fresh ancilla, then use as control (cz instead of ccz)
            gates.append(Gate("ccx", (a, b, anc)))
            gates.append(Gate("cz", (anc, t)))
        elif idx in second_map:
            anc = second_map[idx]
            t = g.qubits[2]
            a, b = g.qubits[0], g.qubits[1]
            gates.append(Gate("cz", (anc, t)))
            # measured uncompute of anc (== a&b at this point)
            gates.append(Gate("h", (anc,)))
            gates.append(Gate("measure", (anc,), cbit=cbit))
            gates.append(Gate("cz", (a, b), cond=cbit))
            gates.append(Gate("reset", (anc,)))
        else:
            gates.append(g)

    new_c = Circuit(new_n, gates, new_nc, c.zero_init)
    return new_c, Req(eps=0.0, ancillas=n_new_anc, measure=True)

"""
measured_uncompute_of_and_ladder_both_directions

Finds pairs of ccz(a,b,t) ... ccz(a,b,t) that share the same control pair (a,b) and
same target t, with a and b both untouched AND with no non-diagonal gate (e.g. H)
applied to t in between (only other cz/ccz gates not involving a conflicting basis
change are allowed, since the ancilla trick turns both ccz into cz(anc,t), which must
commute with everything that happens on t between the two occurrences). A fresh
ancilla anc is set to a&b via one ccx(a,b,anc); both original ccz(a,b,t) become cheap
cz(anc,t) (valid since anc==a&b throughout, a,b untouched); anc is then uncomputed with
the measurement trick: H anc; measure anc -> m; if m==1 apply cz(a,b) classically
controlled; reset anc (Jones/Gidney trick, exact because a,b are unchanged between
compute and uncompute). Net effect per pair: two Toffolis (14T) -> one Toffoli (7T),
with a measurement + classically controlled Clifford correction (0T) replacing the
second Toffoli.
"""
from circuitevolve.circuit import Circuit, Gate
from circuitevolve.verifier import Req


def _find_pairs(c: Circuit):
    """Find disjoint (idx1, idx2, a, b, t) for ccz(a,b,t) ... ccz(a,b,t) where a,b are
    untouched strictly between idx1 and idx2, and t has no non-diagonal gate applied to
    it in that span (only cz/ccz touching t are tolerated, since those commute with the
    cz(anc,t) replacement)."""
    n = len(c.gates)
    used = [False] * n
    pairs = []
    DIAGONAL = {"cz", "ccz", "z", "s", "sdg", "t", "tdg", "rz"}
    for i in range(n):
        if used[i]:
            continue
        g = c.gates[i]
        if g.name != "ccz" or g.cond is not None:
            continue
        a, b, t = g.qubits
        key = frozenset((a, b))
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            if used[j]:
                continue
            h = c.gates[j]
            matched = (
                h.name == "ccz"
                and h.cond is None
                and frozenset((h.qubits[0], h.qubits[1])) == key
                and h.qubits[2] == t
            )
            if matched:
                ok = True
                for k in range(i + 1, j):
                    if used[k]:
                        continue
                    gk = c.gates[k]
                    if a in gk.qubits or b in gk.qubits:
                        ok = False
                        break
                    if t in gk.qubits and gk.name not in DIAGONAL:
                        ok = False
                        break
                if ok:
                    pairs.append((i, j, a, b, t))
                    used[i] = True
                    used[j] = True
                break
            else:
                if a in h.qubits or b in h.qubits:
                    break
                if t in h.qubits and h.name not in DIAGONAL:
                    break
    return pairs


def rewrite(c: Circuit) -> tuple[Circuit, Req]:
    pairs = _find_pairs(c)
    if not pairs:
        return c, Req()

    n_new_anc = len(pairs)
    new_n = c.n + n_new_anc
    new_nc = c.nc + n_new_anc

    first_map = {}
    second_map = {}
    for k, (i1, i2, a, b, t) in enumerate(pairs):
        anc = c.n + k
        cbit = c.nc + k
        first_map[i1] = (a, b, t, anc, cbit)
        second_map[i2] = (a, b, t, anc, cbit)

    gates = []
    for idx, g in enumerate(c.gates):
        if idx in first_map:
            a, b, t, anc, cbit = first_map[idx]
            gates.append(Gate("ccx", (a, b, anc)))
            gates.append(Gate("cz", (anc, t)))
        elif idx in second_map:
            a, b, t, anc, cbit = second_map[idx]
            gates.append(Gate("cz", (anc, t)))
            gates.append(Gate("h", (anc,)))
            gates.append(Gate("measure", (anc,), cbit=cbit))
            gates.append(Gate("cz", (a, b), cond=cbit))
            gates.append(Gate("reset", (anc,)))
        else:
            gates.append(g)

    new_c = Circuit(new_n, gates, new_nc, c.zero_init)
    return new_c, Req(eps=0.0, ancillas=n_new_anc, measure=True)

"""
measured_uncompute_of_and_ladder_both_directions

Generalizes the compute/uncompute-ancilla fusion to *ladder rungs* where the shared
control pair (a,b) of a repeated ccz(a,b,t) is allowed to be touched in between *only
as a control of other diagonal (ccz) gates*, which is exactly what happens inside a
nested AND-ladder (e.g. rung (3,6,7) wraps rung (2,5,6) wraps rung (0,1,5): q6 is a
target of the inner ccz but also reappears as a control of the outer ccz(3,6,7)).
Since ccz is diagonal in the computational basis, using a or b as a control of other
diagonal gates commutes freely with holding anc = a&b; only a *write* to a or b (via a
non-diagonal gate, or as the *target* of a Toffoli/ccz) would invalidate anc, and such
cases are excluded. We hoist each rung's AND value into a fresh ancilla via one ccx,
replace both the first and second ccz(a,b,t) with cz(anc,t) (exact, since anc==a&b
throughout), and uncompute anc with the Jones/Gidney measurement trick: H anc; measure;
classically-controlled cz(a,b) fixup; reset. Pairs are matched innermost-first so that
after an inner rung is rewritten it no longer blocks an outer rung's "a,b untouched"
check (the ccx/cz/measure replacement touches only a,b,t,anc - never changes what the
outer rung sees on its own control pair). Net effect per matched pair: 14T -> 7T.
"""
from circuitevolve.circuit import Circuit, Gate
from circuitevolve.verifier import Req


def _blocks(gk, a, b, t):
    """Does gate gk block treating (a,b) as held / t as control-compatible between the
    two ccz(a,b,t) occurrences of a rung? Allowed: ccz/cz gates that touch a or b only
    as *controls* (never as the ccz target), and diagonal gates on t (t used as control
    of other diagonal gates, or itself untouched). Disallowed: anything else touching
    a, b, or t."""
    DIAGONAL_2 = {"cz"}
    DIAGONAL_3 = {"ccz"}
    touches_a = a in gk.qubits
    touches_b = b in gk.qubits
    touches_t = t in gk.qubits
    if not (touches_a or touches_b or touches_t):
        return False  # fine, no interaction
    if gk.cond is not None:
        return True
    if gk.name in DIAGONAL_3:
        # ccz(x,y,z): a/b may appear only as one of the two "control-like" slots (first
        # two), not as the target (third) slot, since target writes a phase depending on
        # all three and would not disturb a&b's *value* (ccz is diagonal => never writes
        # any qubit's value at all). ccz never changes computational-basis values, so it
        # never invalidates anc = a&b regardless of which slot a/b/t sit in.
        return False
    if gk.name in DIAGONAL_2:
        return False
    if gk.name == "h" and not (touches_a or touches_b or touches_t):
        return False
    # Any non-diagonal single/multi qubit gate (h, x, cx, ccx, swap, rz that isn't
    # diagonal... but rz IS diagonal) touching a,b,t blocks.
    if gk.name == "rz":
        return False
    if gk.name in ("h", "x", "y", "sx", "sxdg", "cx", "ccx", "swap"):
        return True
    return True


def _find_pairs(c: Circuit):
    """Find disjoint (i1, i2, a, b, t) rung-pairs for ccz(a,b,t)...ccz(a,b,t), matching
    innermost (shortest span) first so that already-claimed inner gates (which get
    rewritten to cz/ccx/measure, i.e. diagonal-compatible ops on a,b or benign ops on
    anc) do not block outer rungs relying on the same qubits as controls."""
    n = len(c.gates)
    used = [False] * n
    candidates = []
    for i in range(n):
        g = c.gates[i]
        if g.name != "ccz" or g.cond is not None:
            continue
        a, b, t = g.qubits
        key = frozenset((a, b))
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            h = c.gates[j]
            if h.name == "ccz" and h.cond is None and frozenset((h.qubits[0], h.qubits[1])) == key and h.qubits[2] == t:
                candidates.append((j - i, i, j, a, b, t))
                break
            if _blocks(h, a, b, t):
                break
    candidates.sort()  # shortest span (innermost) first
    pairs = []
    for span, i, j, a, b, t in candidates:
        if used[i] or used[j]:
            continue
        # re-check blocking against only *not yet used* gates, since used gates in this
        # span belong to already-matched inner pairs whose rewritten form (ccx/cz/
        # measure/reset) is diagonal-or-benign w.r.t. a,b,t by construction.
        ok = True
        for k in range(i + 1, j):
            if used[k]:
                continue
            if _blocks(c.gates[k], a, b, t):
                ok = False
                break
        if ok:
            pairs.append((i, j, a, b, t))
            used[i] = True
            used[j] = True
    return pairs


def rewrite(c: Circuit) -> tuple[Circuit, Req]:
    pairs = _find_pairs(c)
    if not pairs:
        return c, Req()

    n_new_anc = len(pairs)
    new_n = c.n + n_new_anc
    new_nc = c.nc + n_new_anc

    first_map = {}
    second_map = {}
    for k, (i1, i2, a, b, t) in enumerate(pairs):
        anc = c.n + k
        cbit = c.nc + k
        first_map[i1] = (a, b, t, anc, cbit)
        second_map[i2] = (a, b, t, anc, cbit)

    gates = []
    for idx, g in enumerate(c.gates):
        if idx in first_map:
            a, b, t, anc, cbit = first_map[idx]
            gates.append(Gate("ccx", (a, b, anc)))
            gates.append(Gate("cz", (anc, t)))
        elif idx in second_map:
            a, b, t, anc, cbit = second_map[idx]
            gates.append(Gate("cz", (anc, t)))
            gates.append(Gate("h", (anc,)))
            gates.append(Gate("measure", (anc,), cbit=cbit))
            gates.append(Gate("cz", (a, b), cond=cbit))
            gates.append(Gate("reset", (anc,)))
        else:
            gates.append(g)

    new_c = Circuit(new_n, gates, new_nc, c.zero_init)
    return new_c, Req(eps=0.0, ancillas=n_new_anc, measure=True)

"""
and_ladder_sharing_across_repeated_blocks: finds control pairs (p, q) used by >= 2 ccz/ccx
(AND-type) gates anywhere in the circuit, where p and q are never touched by ANY other gate
(including other accepted pairs' gates/ancillas) between the first and last such occurrence,
globally across the whole circuit. For each such pair, compute p&q once into a fresh ancilla via
a single Toffoli (ccx(p,q,anc), anc starts at |0>), replace every occurrence's AND-gate by a cheap
cz(ancilla, target) (sound because anc == p&q at every occurrence since p,q are provably untouched
in between), and measurement-uncompute the ancilla once right after the last occurrence (H; measure;
classically-controlled cz(p,q) fixup; reset). ccz is symmetric in its 3 qubits, so for each gate we
only accept pair (p,q) as "the recurring pair" if the third qubit is a genuinely distinct "target"
that is consistently not part of any other accepted pair in this gate; this avoids mis-attributing
roles when the same qubit plays control in one occurrence and target in another. This turns k
occurrences of a shared-pair AND gate (7k T) into one real Toffoli + free CZs + free measurement
uncompute (7 T total).
"""
from circuitevolve.circuit import Circuit, Gate
from circuitevolve.verifier import Req


def _is_and_gate(g: Gate) -> bool:
    return g.name in ("ccx", "ccz")


def rewrite(c: Circuit) -> tuple[Circuit, Req]:
    gates = list(c.gates)
    n_gates = len(gates)

    # For ccx, qubits = (c0, c1, target) -- target role is fixed (the XOR'd qubit).
    # For ccz, qubits are symmetric; we must choose which 2 of the 3 form "the pair" consistently
    # across occurrences. We enumerate candidate pairs by looking at all unordered 2-subsets of
    # each AND gate's qubits, and group occurrences by (gate_name_class, pair) where gate_name_class
    # distinguishes ccx (pair must be exactly (c0,c1)) from ccz (pair can be any 2-subset).
    def and_gate_pair_target_options(g: Gate):
        q0, q1, q2 = g.qubits
        if g.name == "ccx":
            # control pair is fixed: (q0, q1), target is q2 (the XOR target, cannot be treated as control)
            return [(frozenset((q0, q1)), q2)]
        else:  # ccz: symmetric, any 2 of the 3 could be "the pair", third is "target"
            return [
                (frozenset((q0, q1)), q2),
                (frozenset((q0, q2)), q1),
                (frozenset((q1, q2)), q0),
            ]

    # Build occurrence list: for each gate index, list of (pair, target) options.
    options = [and_gate_pair_target_options(g) if _is_and_gate(g) else None for g in gates]

    # Group by pair: occ_by_pair[pair] = list of (gate_idx, target)
    occ_by_pair = {}
    for i, opts in enumerate(options):
        if opts is None:
            continue
        for pair, target in opts:
            occ_by_pair.setdefault(pair, []).append((i, target))

    candidate_pairs = [p for p, occs in occ_by_pair.items() if len(occs) >= 2]
    if not candidate_pairs:
        return c, Req()

    def touches(g: Gate, qset) -> bool:
        return any(q in qset for q in g.qubits)

    # Sort candidates by potential savings (more occurrences first) for greedy selection,
    # since pairs may conflict (share qubits/gates) and we must avoid double-using a gate.
    candidate_pairs.sort(key=lambda p: -len(occ_by_pair[p]))

    used_gate_indices = set()
    accepted = []  # (pair, [(idx, target), ...], first_idx, last_idx)
    reserved_qubits = set()  # qubits used as controls or targets by accepted pairs (to avoid overlap)

    for pair in candidate_pairs:
        occs = occ_by_pair[pair]
        idxs = [i for i, t in occs]
        if any(j in used_gate_indices for j in idxs):
            continue
        p, q = tuple(pair)
        targets = [t for i, t in occs]
        # target must never equal p or q (already guaranteed by construction) and must not be
        # the same qubit as p or q for ANY occurrence (already true); also require all occurrences
        # of this gate index use the SAME pair choice as selected (no gate double-counted under
        # a different pair already accepted).
        first_i, last_i = idxs[0], idxs[-1]

        # Check: p, q untouched by any OTHER gate strictly within [first_i, last_i], where "other"
        # excludes the accepted occurrences themselves (which touch p,q only as controls, consistent
        # with the AND semantics).
        ok = True
        idx_set = set(idxs)
        for j in range(first_i, last_i + 1):
            if j in idx_set:
                continue
            g = gates[j]
            if g is None:
                continue
            if touches(g, (p, q)):
                ok = False
                break
        if not ok:
            continue

        # Also ensure no conflict: none of these gate indices have already been claimed for a
        # DIFFERENT pair selection, and the targets of these occurrences are not themselves p/q
        # of some other accepted pair in a way that would be corrupted. We conservatively require
        # that p and q are not used as a "target" qubit by any other accepted pair's occurrences
        # inside [first_i, last_i], and vice versa -- simplest safe check: p,q must not overlap
        # reserved_qubits from previously accepted (disjoint) pairs AT ALL (fully disjoint pairs
        # only, to keep composition trivially safe).
        if p in reserved_qubits or q in reserved_qubits:
            continue

        accepted.append((pair, occs, first_i, last_i))
        used_gate_indices.update(idxs)
        reserved_qubits.add(p)
        reserved_qubits.add(q)

    if not accepted:
        return c, Req()

    # Re-check: ensure accepted pairs' windows don't let one pair's ancilla-compute/uncompute
    # scaffolding collide with another pair's gates on the SAME qubit set (targets may overlap
    # across different pairs' gates, that's fine -- cz commutes and only acts when anc is set).
    # Since p,q (reserved_qubits) are globally disjoint across accepted pairs, and ancillas are
    # fresh, this is safe regardless of target overlaps.

    new_n = c.n
    new_nc = c.nc
    pair_ancilla = {}
    pair_cbit = {}
    pair_first_idx = {}
    pair_last_idx = {}
    pair_occ_idx_set = {}

    for pair, occs, first_i, last_i in accepted:
        pair_ancilla[pair] = new_n
        new_n += 1
        pair_cbit[pair] = new_nc
        new_nc += 1
        pair_first_idx[pair] = first_i
        pair_last_idx[pair] = last_i
        pair_occ_idx_set[pair] = set(i for i, t in occs)

    # Map gate index -> (pair, target) for accepted occurrences
    idx_to_pair_target = {}
    for pair, occs, first_i, last_i in accepted:
        for i, t in occs:
            idx_to_pair_target[i] = (pair, t)

    new_gates = []
    for i, g in enumerate(gates):
        if i in idx_to_pair_target:
            pair, target = idx_to_pair_target[i]
            anc = pair_ancilla[pair]
            p, q = tuple(pair)
            if i == pair_first_idx[pair]:
                new_gates.append(Gate("ccx", (p, q, anc)))
            new_gates.append(Gate("cz", (anc, target)))
            if i == pair_last_idx[pair]:
                cbit = pair_cbit[pair]
                new_gates.append(Gate("h", (anc,)))
                new_gates.append(Gate("measure", (anc,), cbit=cbit))
                new_gates.append(Gate("cz", (p, q), cond=cbit))
                new_gates.append(Gate("reset", (anc,)))
        else:
            new_gates.append(g)

    new_c = Circuit(new_n, new_gates, new_nc, c.zero_init)
    n_ancillas = len(accepted)
    return new_c, Req(eps=0.0, ancillas=n_ancillas, measure=True)

"""ccz_to_relative_phase_toffoli_in_uncomputed_pairs

Replaces exactly-matched compute/uncompute ccz pairs (same three qubits, identical
gate, with only diagonal gates touching the target in between) with Maslov/Jones
relative-phase Toffoli (RTOF) implementations costing 4 T each instead of 7 T.
This is exact: the RTOF differs from CCZ by extra relative phases on non-|111>-
reachable branches of the compute step, but since every gate strictly between the
compute and uncompute acts diagonally (commutes with phases) and the uncompute step
applies the exact inverse relative-phase circuit, those spurious phases cancel
identically, leaving the overall unitary on (c0,c1,t) and the enclosed region exactly
as before.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import replace as dc_replace

from circuitevolve.circuit import Circuit, Gate
from circuitevolve.verifier import Req


def _rtof4t_ccz(qubits):
    """4T relative-phase Toffoli equivalent (up to relative phase) to ccz(c0,c1,t),
    built from Maslov's construction using H-conjugation around a cz-type core.
    Sequence (Jones 2012 relative-phase Toffoli), expressed directly as a CCZ-like
    diagonal-up-to-phase operator on (c0,c1,t):
        h t; t c0; t c1; t t; cx c0,c1; cx t,c0; cx c1,t;
        tdg c0; cx c1,c0; tdg c1; tdg c0; cx t,c0; cx c1,t; cx c0,c1; h t
    This is the standard 4T relative-phase Toffoli pattern used in surface-code
    compilations (Jones, "Low-overhead constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli
    gate", 2013), re-targeted here to realize ccz (control-control-Z) instead of ccx
    by dropping the outer H conjugation on the target that turns X-type into Z-type.
    """
    c0, c1, t = qubits
    return [
        Gate("h", (t,)),
        Gate("t", (c0,)),
        Gate("t", (c1,)),
        Gate("t", (t,)),
        Gate("cx", (c0, c1)),
        Gate("cx", (t, c0)),
        Gate("cx", (c1, t)),
        Gate("tdg", (c0,)),
        Gate("cx", (c1, c0)),
        Gate("tdg", (c1,)),
        Gate("tdg", (c0,)),
        Gate("cx", (t, c0)),
        Gate("cx", (c1, t)),
        Gate("cx", (c0, c1)),
        Gate("h", (t,)),
    ]


def _rtof4t_ccz_dagger(qubits):
    """Inverse of _rtof4t_ccz: reverse gate order, invert each gate (t<->tdg, h/cx self-inverse)."""
    fwd = _rtof4t_ccz(qubits)
    inv_name = {"t": "tdg", "tdg": "t", "h": "h", "cx": "cx"}
    return [dc_replace(g, name=inv_name[g.name]) for g in reversed(fwd)]


def _is_diagonal_use(g: Gate, qset: frozenset) -> bool:
    """True if gate g, touching one of the protected qubits in qset, is diagonal
    (so it commutes with any relative phase living on the computational basis)."""
    diag_names = {"z", "s", "sdg", "t", "tdg", "rz", "cz", "ccz"}
    if not (set(g.qubits) & qset):
        return True  # doesn't touch protected qubits at all
    return g.name in diag_names


def rewrite(c: Circuit) -> tuple[Circuit, Req]:
    gates = list(c.gates)
    n = len(gates)
    used = [False] * n

    # find matched ccz(a,b,t)...ccz(a,b,t) pairs (same qubit triple, exact match),
    # where every gate strictly between acts on {a,b,t} only diagonally, and a,b are
    # completely untouched in between (so the pair really is compute/uncompute of a
    # phase kick controlled by a&b, acting diagonally on the enclosed region).
    pairs = []  # (i, j) indices into gates
    for i in range(n):
        if used[i] or gates[i].name != "ccz":
            continue
        qi = gates[i].qubits
        qset = frozenset(qi)
        ab = frozenset(qi[:2])
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            if used[j]:
                continue
            g = gates[j]
            if g.name == "ccz" and frozenset(g.qubits) == qset:
                # check everything strictly between i and j
                ok = True
                for k in range(i + 1, j):
                    if used[k]:
                        continue
                    gk = gates[k]
                    if set(gk.qubits) & ab:
                        # a or b touched by a non-trivial gate other than as part of
                        # another matched ccz on the exact same pair -> not safe
                        ok = False
                        break
                    if not _is_diagonal_use(gk, qset):
                        ok = False
                        break
                if ok:
                    pairs.append((i, j))
                    used[i] = True
                    used[j] = True
                break  # only match the nearest valid partner for gate i

    if not pairs:
        return c, Req()

    new_gates = []
    for idx, g in enumerate(gates):
        matched = None
        for (i, j) in pairs:
            if idx == i:
                matched = ("fwd", (i, j))
                break
            if idx == j:
                matched = ("bwd", (i, j))
                break
        if matched is None:
            new_gates.append(g)
            continue
        kind, (i, j) = matched
        qubits = gates[i].qubits
        if kind == "fwd":
            new_gates.extend(_rtof4t_ccz(qubits))
        else:
            new_gates.extend(_rtof4t_ccz_dagger(qubits))

    new_c = Circuit(c.n, new_gates, c.nc, c.zero_init)
    return new_c, Req(eps=0.0, ancillas=0, measure=False)

"""ccz_to_relative_phase_toffoli_in_uncomputed_pairs

Finds H-conjugated CCZ pairs h(t); ccz(a,b,t); ...; ccz(a,b,t); h(t) that realize a
CCX(a,b,t) compute ... CCX(a,b,t) uncompute (matched on the same qubit triple), where
everything strictly between the two CCX-equivalent blocks only uses the target qubit t
diagonally (never as a control feeding back into a,b) and leaves a,b completely alone.
Each such CCX is replaced by a Maslov/Jones relative-phase Toffoli (RTOF, 4T instead of
7T for ccx/ccz). This is exact because the RTOF differs from CCX only by relative phases
on basis states that are never reached as |1,1,*> during the compute half; the enclosed
diagonal gates commute with any computational-basis phase, so those spurious phases are
exactly undone by the daggered RTOF at the uncompute step, leaving the net action on
(a,b,t) and the enclosed region identical to the original CCZ...CCZ circuit.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import replace as dc_replace

from circuitevolve.circuit import Circuit, Gate
from circuitevolve.verifier import Req


def _rtof4t_ccx(qubits):
    """4T relative-phase Toffoli (Jones 2012 / Maslov), realizes CCX(c0,c1,t) up to a
    relative phase of -1 on the |c0=0,c1=1,t> and |c0=1,c1=0,t> branches (which cancel
    exactly when paired with its own dagger around a diagonal-only enclosed region)."""
    c0, c1, t = qubits
    return [
        Gate("h", (t,)),
        Gate("t", (c0,)),
        Gate("t", (c1,)),
        Gate("t", (t,)),
        Gate("cx", (c0, c1)),
        Gate("cx", (t, c0)),
        Gate("cx", (c1, t)),
        Gate("tdg", (c0,)),
        Gate("cx", (c1, c0)),
        Gate("tdg", (c1,)),
        Gate("tdg", (c0,)),
        Gate("cx", (t, c0)),
        Gate("cx", (c1, t)),
        Gate("cx", (c0, c1)),
        Gate("h", (t,)),
    ]


def _rtof4t_ccx_dagger(qubits):
    fwd = _rtof4t_ccx(qubits)
    inv_name = {"t": "tdg", "tdg": "t", "h": "h", "cx": "cx"}
    return [dc_replace(g, name=inv_name[g.name]) for g in reversed(fwd)]


def _find_hczh_blocks(gates):
    """Find indices i such that gates[i-1] = h(t), gates[i] = ccz(a,b,t), gates[i+1] = h(t)
    for some ordering of (a,b,t) matching the ccz's qubits (t = the one H'd on both sides).
    Returns list of (h_before_idx, ccz_idx, h_after_idx, (a,b,t))."""
    n = len(gates)
    blocks = []
    for i in range(n):
        g = gates[i]
        if g.name != "ccz":
            continue
        if i - 1 < 0 or i + 1 >= n:
            continue
        gb, ga = gates[i - 1], gates[i + 1]
        if gb.name != "h" or ga.name != "h":
            continue
        if gb.qubits != ga.qubits:
            continue
        t = gb.qubits[0]
        if t not in g.qubits:
            continue
        others = tuple(q for q in g.qubits if q != t)
        if len(others) != 2:
            continue
        a, b = others
        blocks.append((i - 1, i, i + 1, (a, b, t)))
    return blocks


def _is_diagonal_use(g: Gate, qset: frozenset) -> bool:
    diag_names = {"z", "s", "sdg", "t", "tdg", "rz", "cz", "ccz"}
    if not (set(g.qubits) & qset):
        return True
    return g.name in diag_names


def rewrite(c: Circuit) -> tuple[Circuit, Req]:
    gates = list(c.gates)
    n = len(gates)

    blocks = _find_hczh_blocks(gates)
    if not blocks:
        return c, Req()

    # consumed[i] marks a gate index that belongs to a matched block's h/ccz/h triple
    consumed = [False] * n
    used_block = [False] * len(blocks)

    pairs = []  # (block_i_index, block_j_index) matched compute/uncompute pairs
    for bi in range(len(blocks)):
        if used_block[bi]:
            continue
        hb_i, cz_i, ha_i, trip_i = blocks[bi]
        if consumed[hb_i] or consumed[cz_i] or consumed[ha_i]:
            continue
        qset_i = frozenset(trip_i)
        ab_i = frozenset(trip_i[:2])
        for bj in range(bi + 1, len(blocks)):
            if used_block[bj]:
                continue
            hb_j, cz_j, ha_j, trip_j = blocks[bj]
            if consumed[hb_j] or consumed[cz_j] or consumed[ha_j]:
                continue
            if frozenset(trip_j) != qset_i:
                continue
            # check region strictly between the two CCX-equivalent blocks: from ha_i+1
            # (after first H) up to hb_j-1 (before second H) must only touch {a,b,t}
            # diagonally and must never touch a,b at all (keeps a&b value stable),
            # while t may be touched only via diagonal gates (phase-kick usage).
            ok = True
            for k in range(ha_i + 1, hb_j):
                if consumed[k]:
                    continue
                gk = gates[k]
                if set(gk.qubits) & ab_i:
                    ok = False
                    break
                if not _is_diagonal_use(gk, qset_i):
                    ok = False
                    break
            if ok:
                pairs.append((bi, bj))
                used_block[bi] = True
                used_block[bj] = True
                consumed[hb_i] = consumed[cz_i] = consumed[ha_i] = True
                consumed[hb_j] = consumed[cz_j] = consumed[ha_j] = True
                break

    if not pairs:
        return c, Req()

    # Build replacement: for each matched block, replace its h/ccz/h triple with the
    # RTOF (forward for the first occurrence, dagger for the second); drop the H's
    # since the RTOF construction already begins/ends with H on the target internally
    # equivalent to the same basis change (h; ccz; h == ccx, and our RTOF directly
    # implements ccx, including its own internal H's on t).
    replace_as = {}  # block_index -> "fwd" | "bwd"
    for (bi, bj) in pairs:
        replace_as[bi] = "fwd"
        replace_as[bj] = "bwd"

    idx_to_block = {}
    for bidx, (hb, cz, ha, trip) in enumerate(blocks):
        if bidx in replace_as:
            idx_to_block[hb] = (bidx, "start")
            idx_to_block[cz] = (bidx, "mid")
            idx_to_block[ha] = (bidx, "end")

    new_gates = []
    skip_until = -1
    i = 0
    while i < n:
        if i in idx_to_block:
            bidx, role = idx_to_block[i]
            if role == "start":
                hb, cz, ha, trip = blocks[bidx]
                kind = replace_as[bidx]
                if kind == "fwd":
                    new_gates.extend(_rtof4t_ccx(trip))
                else:
                    new_gates.extend(_rtof4t_ccx_dagger(trip))
                i = ha + 1
                continue
            else:
                # mid/end should never be reached directly due to jump above
                i += 1
                continue
        else:
            new_gates.append(gates[i])
            i += 1

    new_c = Circuit(c.n, new_gates, c.nc, c.zero_init)
    return new_c, Req(eps=0.0, ancillas=0, measure=False)

"""ccz_to_relative_phase_toffoli_in_uncomputed_pairs

Replaces a compute/uncompute pair of identical-triple CCZ/CCX gates (each H-conjugated
into an effective CCX on the same (a,b,t) triple) by Maslov/Jones 4T relative-phase
Toffolis (RTOF), PROVIDED the enclosed region never touches a or b and only ever uses t
as a CONTROL of diagonal gates (so t's computational-basis value, and hence any relative
phase RTOF attaches to basis states, is carried unchanged and only ever contributes
global/diagonal phases that commute through the enclosed region). Under that condition
RTOF_fwd ... RTOF_fwd^dagger reproduces CCX ... CCX exactly on the touched qubits: the
spurious relative phase that RTOF adds to the |a,b,t> computational basis state is a
*function of that same basis state* (since a,b,t are not modified again until the
uncompute), and it is exactly cancelled by the conjugate phase of RTOF^dagger, because no
enclosed gate ever conditions a *different* qubit's amplitude on the extra phase (the
enclosed gates are all diagonal in the computational basis of a,b,t, hence commute with
any phase attached to a computational basis state of a,b,t).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import replace as dc_replace

from circuitevolve.circuit import Circuit, Gate
from circuitevolve.verifier import Req


def _rtof4t_ccx(qubits):
    """4T relative-phase Toffoli (Jones 2012 / Maslov), realizes CCX(c0,c1,t) up to a
    diagonal relative phase that depends only on the computational basis state of
    (c0,c1,t) (no superposition-mixing beyond ordinary CCX action)."""
    c0, c1, t = qubits
    return [
        Gate("h", (t,)),
        Gate("t", (c0,)),
        Gate("t", (c1,)),
        Gate("t", (t,)),
        Gate("cx", (c0, c1)),
        Gate("cx", (t, c0)),
        Gate("cx", (c1, t)),
        Gate("tdg", (c0,)),
        Gate("cx", (c1, c0)),
        Gate("tdg", (c1,)),
        Gate("tdg", (c0,)),
        Gate("cx", (t, c0)),
        Gate("cx", (c1, t)),
        Gate("cx", (c0, c1)),
        Gate("h", (t,)),
    ]


_INV_NAME = {"t": "tdg", "tdg": "t", "h": "h", "cx": "cx"}


def _rtof4t_ccx_dagger(qubits):
    fwd = _rtof4t_ccx(qubits)
    return [dc_replace(g, name=_INV_NAME[g.name]) for g in reversed(fwd)]


_DIAG_NAMES = {"z", "s", "sdg", "t", "tdg", "rz", "cz", "ccz"}


def _find_hczh_blocks(gates):
    """Find i with gates[i-1]=h(t), gates[i]=ccz(...,t,...), gates[i+1]=h(t) (same t)."""
    n = len(gates)
    blocks = []
    for i in range(n):
        g = gates[i]
        if g.name != "ccz":
            continue
        if i - 1 < 0 or i + 1 >= n:
            continue
        gb, ga = gates[i - 1], gates[i + 1]
        if gb.name != "h" or ga.name != "h":
            continue
        if gb.qubits != ga.qubits:
            continue
        t = gb.qubits[0]
        if t not in g.qubits:
            continue
        others = tuple(q for q in g.qubits if q != t)
        if len(others) != 2:
            continue
        a, b = others
        blocks.append((i - 1, i, i + 1, (a, b, t)))
    return blocks


def rewrite(c: Circuit) -> tuple[Circuit, Req]:
    gates = list(c.gates)
    n = len(gates)

    blocks = _find_hczh_blocks(gates)
    if not blocks:
        return c, Req()

    consumed = [False] * n
    used_block = [False] * len(blocks)
    pairs = []

    for bi in range(len(blocks)):
        if used_block[bi]:
            continue
        hb_i, cz_i, ha_i, trip_i = blocks[bi]
        if consumed[hb_i] or consumed[cz_i] or consumed[ha_i]:
            continue
        qset_i = frozenset(trip_i)
        a_i, b_i, t_i = trip_i
        ab_i = frozenset((a_i, b_i))

        for bj in range(bi + 1, len(blocks)):
            if used_block[bj]:
                continue
            hb_j, cz_j, ha_j, trip_j = blocks[bj]
            if consumed[hb_j] or consumed[cz_j] or consumed[ha_j]:
                continue
            if frozenset(trip_j) != qset_i:
                continue
            if trip_j != trip_i:
                # require identical (a,b,t) role assignment, not just same set,
                # so "t" (the H-conjugated qubit) matches on both ends
                continue

            # Strict condition for exactness: between the two blocks, a and b must
            # never be touched at all, and t must only ever appear as a control of a
            # strictly-diagonal gate (never as the target of anything, never inside
            # another H-conjugated block, never as a control feeding a non-diagonal
            # gate). This guarantees t's computational-basis value is frozen and only
            # ever triggers diagonal (phase) operations, so the RTOF's extra relative
            # phase - itself a function only of (a,b,t)'s basis value - commutes
            # through untouched and cancels exactly against RTOF^dagger.
            ok = True
            for k in range(ha_i + 1, hb_j):
                if consumed[k]:
                    continue
                gk = gates[k]
                qk = set(gk.qubits)
                if qk & ab_i:
                    ok = False
                    break
                if t_i in qk:
                    if gk.name not in _DIAG_NAMES:
                        ok = False
                        break
                    if gk.name in ("rz",) and gk.cond is not None:
                        ok = False
                        break
                    if gk.cond is not None:
                        ok = False
                        break
            if not ok:
                continue

            pairs.append((bi, bj))
            used_block[bi] = True
            used_block[bj] = True
            consumed[hb_i] = consumed[cz_i] = consumed[ha_i] = True
            consumed[hb_j] = consumed[cz_j] = consumed[ha_j] = True
            break

    if not pairs:
        return c, Req()

    replace_as = {}
    for (bi, bj) in pairs:
        replace_as[bi] = "fwd"
        replace_as[bj] = "bwd"

    idx_to_start = {}
    for bidx, (hb, cz, ha, trip) in enumerate(blocks):
        if bidx in replace_as:
            idx_to_start[hb] = (bidx, ha)

    new_gates = []
    i = 0
    while i < n:
        if i in idx_to_start:
            bidx, ha = idx_to_start[i]
            hb, cz, ha2, trip = blocks[bidx]
            kind = replace_as[bidx]
            if kind == "fwd":
                new_gates.extend(_rtof4t_ccx(trip))
            else:
                new_gates.extend(_rtof4t_ccx_dagger(trip))
            i = ha + 1
            continue
        else:
            new_gates.append(gates[i])
            i += 1

    new_c = Circuit(c.n, new_gates, c.nc, c.zero_init)
    return new_c, Req(eps=0.0, ancillas=0, measure=False)

ideas.name: temporary_and_ancilla_for_conjugated_control_pair
ideas.idea: Generalize the existing repeated-control-pair fusion so that the shared control pair is allowed to be CNOT-conjugated between uses instead of strictly untouched. Pattern: ccz(p,q,t1) ... cx(p,q) ... ccz(p',q,t2) where the intervening Clifford on the control wires is a known CNOT/CX network. Track the control pair symbolically through the CX network as a pair of linear forms over GF(2); if the AND of the two forms at use-1 equals (up to a CX-expressible relabeling of which wire holds which form) the AND at use-2, allocate a fresh ancilla a, compute a = (first AND) once with a single ccx, replace BOTH ccz's by cz(a,t) (free), and uncompute a with the Jones/Gidney measured uncompute (H a; measure; classically-controlled fixup CZ on the current control wires; reset). The key extra mechanism over the playbook rule is the GF(2) linear-form tracking of the controls through the cx layers, which lets pairs that are *not* literally identical be identified. In this circuit the cx q[1],q[2] / cx q[4],q[5] / cx q[7],q[8] gates sit exactly between the paired ccz's, and after tracking, ccz(1,2,3) with ccz(1,2,3) at the end (separated by cx(1,2) ... cx(1,2)) and the ccz(4,5,6)/ccz(4,5,6) pair (separated by cx(4,5) ... cx(4,5)) become genuinely shared AND terms; so do ccz(3,5,6) and the later ccz(3,5,6). Note the AND itself is only invariant when the conjugation maps the control subspace back to itself, which the mirrored cx structure here does.
ideas.where: The mirrored ccz pairs: ccz(1,2,3) at the start vs ccz(1,2,3) near the end (with cx(1,2) between, applied twice = identity on the control pair); ccz(3,5,6) early vs ccz(3,5,6) late; ccz(4,5,6) early vs ccz(4,5,6) late; ccz(7,8,9) vs ccz(6,8,9) (controls q[8] conjugated by cx(7,8) and cx(6,8)).

ideas.name: and_sharing_across_mirror_via_persistent_ancilla
ideas.idea: This circuit is a compute / act / mirrored-uncompute sandwich (the whole q3/q6/q9 block is palindromic around the middle). Instead of fusing pairs locally, detect the global mirror symmetry: find the longest prefix P and suffix S such that S is the gate-reverse of P modulo the Hadamard conjugations and the CX relabelings, with a 'core' C in the middle. Then every AND term consumed in P is consumed again in S. Hold the AND values in a register of fresh ancillas across the core: for each distinct AND term (p&q), compute it ONCE with a single ccx into a dedicated clean ancilla at its first occurrence in P, use cz(a,t) at every occurrence in both P and S (0 T), and measured-uncompute all of them at the end (0 T). This differs from pairwise fusion because it amortizes a single compute across an arbitrary number of occurrences and tolerates the controls being touched in the core, as long as the linear forms are restored by the mirror (which the mirror guarantees by construction). Requires a verification pass that the control wires' GF(2) state at the suffix occurrence equals that at the prefix occurrence; if the core modifies them irreversibly the rule declines. Up to ~4 distinct AND terms here, each going from 14 T to 7 T, and the three H-conjugated layers keep the ancillas classical so the trick is legal.

ideas.name: measured_uncompute_of_relative_phase_toffoli_chain
ideas.idea: Where a Toffoli's target is subsequently only ever hit by diagonal gates (cz/cp/rz) and is finally uncomputed or measured in the X basis, the exact Toffoli can be replaced by a *relative-phase* Toffoli (Maslov's 4-T / Jones' 4-T temporary-AND construction) because the spurious relative phases cancel against the matching uncompute, and the H+measure uncompute is phase-insensitive on the branch that is discarded. Pattern: ccx(c0,c1,a) with a a fresh-or-provably-|0> ancilla, a used only as control of diagonal gates, then uncomputed by measured-uncompute (which the playbook rules have already installed here, and which this rule chains onto). Replace the remaining real compute ccx by the 4-T temporary-AND; the measured uncompute stays 0 T. This stacks multiplicatively with the two ancilla-fusion rules above: every compute-AND they leave behind drops 7 T -> 4 T. Applies directly to the existing ccx q[0],q[2],q[10] / measured-uncompute pattern already present in the circuit, and to every ancilla introduced by the fusion rules. Must be guarded so TKET peephole does not resynthesize the 4-T AND back into an exact Toffoli (emit it as explicit h/t/tdg/cx so FullPeepholeOptimise sees only Clifford+T and cannot inflate it).
ideas.where: ccx q[0],q[2],q[10] paired with the existing h q[10]; measure; if(c[0]==1) cz q[0],q[2]; reset q[10] block; plus each compute-AND emitted by the two rules above.
