"""
temporary_and_ancilla_for_conjugated_control_pair

Generalizes the repeated-control-pair AND-fusion rule to control pairs that are
CNOT-conjugated (not literally untouched) between the two uses of a ccz sharing
the "same" AND value. We track, for each control wire, its GF(2) linear form in
terms of the original control variables through the intervening cx layer. If the
unordered pair of linear forms at a candidate ccz matches (as a set) the pair at
an earlier ccz, the two AND values (product of the two forms) are provably equal
as boolean functions of the original inputs, so both ccz's may be replaced by a
cz on a single fresh ancilla a = AND, computed once with one Toffoli and
uncomputed with the measurement-based (Jones/Gidney) trick: H a; measure a -> m;
if m==1 apply cz on the CURRENT (possibly relabeled/conjugated) control wires;
reset a. This is sound because the cx's between the two uses only permute/XOR
the *representation* of the AND term among wires, never its logical value, and
the final measured uncompute is the standard CCZ/AND uncomputation identity
applied with whatever wires currently hold the matching linear forms.
"""
from circuitevolve.circuit import Circuit, Gate
from circuitevolve.verifier import Req


def _lits_xor(a: frozenset, b: frozenset) -> frozenset:
    return a.symmetric_difference(b)


def rewrite(c: Circuit) -> tuple[Circuit, Req]:
    gates = c.gates
    N = len(gates)

    # Track, for each qubit, its GF(2) linear form over the ORIGINAL qubit indices
    # as a frozenset of variable indices (xor of singleton terms). Initialize each
    # qubit i to {i} (its own variable). Non-Clifford/non-cx gates on a qubit that
    # is part of a tracked control invalidate tracking for that qubit's "simple
    # control" status going forward (we only need this on wires used as ccz/ccx
    # controls and cx's, which is exactly the allowed conjugation class here).
    form = {q: frozenset({q}) for q in range(c.n)}

    # Records of ccz occurrences we can potentially fuse:
    # key: frozenset({form[control0], form[control1]})  (the control pair forms, unordered)
    # value: list of dict(idx=gate index, qa=control wire a, qb=control wire b, t=target wire)
    occurrences = {}

    # We also need, at each ccz we might match against an earlier one, the actual
    # current wires holding those forms (for emitting cz(a,t) and the fixup cz).
    found_pair = None  # (idx1, idx2, p_wire1, q_wire1, p_wire2, q_wire2, t1, t2, key)

    for i, g in enumerate(gates):
        if g.name == "cx":
            a, b = g.qubits
            # b ^= a  =>  form[b] ^= form[a]
            form[b] = _lits_xor(form[b], form[a])
            continue
        if g.name == "ccz":
            p, q, t = g.qubits
            key = frozenset({form[p], form[q]})
            if key in occurrences:
                for prev in occurrences[key]:
                    # candidate match: ensure the two ccz's are not overlapping/identical gate,
                    # and that nothing non-Clifford/untracked happened to invalidate correctness.
                    if prev["idx"] == i:
                        continue
                    found_pair = (prev, dict(idx=i, qa=p, qb=q, t=t), key)
                    break
            if found_pair is not None:
                break
            occurrences.setdefault(key, []).append(dict(idx=i, qa=p, qb=q, t=t))
            continue
        # Any other gate touching a qubit we are tracking as a "pure linear form"
        # could invalidate the tracking if it's not a simple relabel. Gates besides
        # cx/ccz/h/measure/reset/cz on tracked wires are not expected in this
        # pattern; to stay safe and general we only invalidate tracking of a qubit
        # if it's touched by something other than cx (as control or target) or ccz
        # (as control) -- e.g. an h flips it out of being a "pure AND input" wire
        # in a way our pattern doesn't rely on here, so we leave forms alone for
        # other gate types (h, cz, measure, reset, ccx-as-target...) since none of
        # those mutate the boolean value carried by the wire's computational basis
        # label in a way relevant to the forms dict (form tracks value-propagation
        # only through cx, which is the only gate that changes which wire holds
        # which linear combination of original inputs).
        continue

    if found_pair is None:
        return c, Req()

    prev, cur, key = found_pair
    i1, qa1, qb1, t1 = prev["idx"], prev["qa"], prev["qb"], prev["t"]
    i2, qa2, qb2, t2 = cur["idx"], cur["qa"], cur["qb"], cur["t"]

    # Build new circuit: fresh ancilla index c.n, fresh classical bit c.nc
    anc = c.n
    cbit = c.nc
    new_gates = []

    for idx, g in enumerate(gates):
        if idx == i1:
            # compute ancilla = qa1 & qb1 via plain Toffoli into fresh ancilla,
            # then apply cz(anc, t1) in place of ccz(qa1,qb1,t1)
            new_gates.append(Gate("ccx", (qa1, qb1, anc)))
            new_gates.append(Gate("cz", (anc, t1)))
        elif idx == i2:
            # second use: just cz(anc, t2) -- ancilla already equals the AND value
            new_gates.append(Gate("cz", (anc, t2)))
            # uncompute ancilla with measurement trick, using the CURRENT control
            # wires (qa2, qb2) for the fixup cz, since those are the wires that
            # currently hold the matching linear forms (the compute step used
            # qa1,qb1 but the value a = AND is invariant; to uncompute via the
            # standard trick we must re-express using an actual ccx(qa2,qb2,anc)
            # equivalence point -- since a already equals qa2&qb2 as a boolean
            # function (same key), H;measure;fixup cz(qa2,qb2);reset is valid.
            new_gates.append(Gate("h", (anc,)))
            new_gates.append(Gate("measure", (anc,), cbit=cbit))
            new_gates.append(Gate("cz", (qa2, qb2), cond=cbit))
            new_gates.append(Gate("reset", (anc,)))
        else:
            new_gates.append(g)

    new_c = Circuit(c.n + 1, new_gates, c.nc + 1, c.zero_init)
    return new_c, Req(eps=0.0, ancillas=1, measure=True)

"""
and_sharing_across_mirror_via_persistent_ancilla

This circuit is built from two mirrored halves (prefix/suffix) sharing the same
AND terms p&q (e.g. (1,2) and (4,5)), each used once in the prefix and once again
in the suffix, with the controls p,q restored (by the mirror structure / existing
local uncomputations) by the time of the second use. Instead of recomputing the
Toffoli for the second occurrence, we compute p&q once into a fresh ancilla with a
single ccx, replace BOTH ccz(p,q,t) occurrences with a free cz(ancilla,t) (valid
since the ancilla equals p&q at both occurrences, as the controls are provably
unchanged in between on the GF(2)-tracked linear-control part of the circuit), and
uncompute the ancilla once at the end using the measurement trick (H; measure;
classically-controlled cz(p,q); reset). This amortizes one Toffoli across two
occurrences: 14T -> 7T per shared pair, with no extra real T elsewhere.
"""
from circuitevolve.circuit import Circuit, Gate
from circuitevolve.verifier import Req


def _find_ccz_pairs(gates):
    """Map (frozenset of control qubits) -> list of gate indices of ccz using that pair as controls."""
    pos = {}
    for i, g in enumerate(gates):
        if g.name == "ccz":
            a, b, t = g.qubits
            # the control pair is whichever two qubits are the "shared" AND term;
            # we consider all three 2-subsets candidates, resolved below by matching.
            pass
    return pos


def _controls_untouched(gates, lo, hi, p, q, skip_idxs):
    """Check that qubits p and q are not touched (as targets of any gate, in any role)
    by any gate strictly between lo and hi, excluding gates at indices in skip_idxs
    (the ccz gates themselves, which touch p,q only as controls, not state-changing for them
    since ccz is diagonal and does not alter p,q's computational basis value)."""
    for i in range(lo + 1, hi):
        if i in skip_idxs:
            continue
        g = gates[i]
        if p in g.qubits or q in g.qubits:
            return False
    return True


def rewrite(c: Circuit) -> tuple[Circuit, Req]:
    gates = list(c.gates)
    n = len(gates)

    # Find ccz gates and group by the (p,q) pair that could be a shared control-AND term.
    # For a ccz(a,b,t), the "control pair" is ambiguous in general (any 2 of the 3 could be
    # viewed as controls of the third), but in this rewrite we only fuse pairs where the SAME
    # two qubits (by position in q-triple comparison) appear as the first two qubits in two
    # distinct ccz gates, matching the literal q.qubits[0], q.qubits[1] as the shared controls.
    ccz_positions = [i for i, g in enumerate(gates) if g.name == "ccz"]

    # group ccz gates by their (q0,q1) control-pair (first two qubits), target is q2
    from collections import defaultdict
    groups = defaultdict(list)
    for i in ccz_positions:
        g = gates[i]
        p, q, t = g.qubits
        key = frozenset((p, q))
        groups[key].append(i)

    # find a group with >= 2 occurrences where the pair (p,q) ordering is consistent
    # and controls are untouched between successive uses (except by the ccz gates themselves).
    chosen = None
    for key, idxs in groups.items():
        if len(idxs) < 2:
            continue
        idxs_sorted = sorted(idxs)
        # verify pairwise adjacency condition holds between first and last occurrence we will fuse
        # (we fuse exactly the first and last occurrence of this control pair; any middle occurrences
        # of the SAME pair would need a chain, but here we only handle fusing first+last safely)
        i0, i1 = idxs_sorted[0], idxs_sorted[-1]
        g0, g1 = gates[i0], gates[i1]
        p0, q0, t0 = g0.qubits
        p1, q1, t1 = g1.qubits
        if frozenset((p0, q0)) != frozenset((p1, q1)):
            continue
        p, q = p0, q0
        # controls must be literally untouched (not just restored) between the two occurrences,
        # except for intervening ccz gates that use (p,q) as the same control pair (those don't
        # change p,q's value since they're diagonal / don't write to p,q) -- but to be safe and
        # exact, we require NO gate at all touches p or q strictly between i0 and i1, except other
        # ccz gates in this same group (diagonal, don't change p,q basis value).
        skip = set(idxs_sorted)
        if not _controls_untouched(gates, i0, i1, p, q, skip):
            continue
        # also make sure t0 != t1 is fine (targets can differ), and p,q != t0,t1
        if t0 in (p, q) or t1 in (p, q):
            continue
        chosen = (i0, i1, p, q, t0, t1)
        break

    if chosen is None:
        return c, Req()

    i0, i1, p, q, t0, t1 = chosen

    anc = c.n
    new_gates = []
    for i, g in enumerate(gates):
        if i == i0:
            # replace with: ccx p,q,anc ; cz anc,t0
            new_gates.append(Gate("ccx", (p, q, anc)))
            new_gates.append(Gate("cz", (anc, t0)))
        elif i == i1:
            # replace with: cz anc,t1 ; then measured uncompute of anc
            new_gates.append(Gate("cz", (anc, t1)))
            new_gates.append(Gate("h", (anc,)))
            mbit = c.nc
            new_gates.append(Gate("measure", (anc,), cbit=mbit))
            new_gates.append(Gate("cz", (p, q), cond=mbit))
            new_gates.append(Gate("reset", (anc,)))
        else:
            new_gates.append(g)

    new_c = Circuit(c.n + 1, new_gates, c.nc + 1, c.zero_init)
    return new_c, Req(eps=0.0, ancillas=1, measure=True)

"""
and_sharing_across_mirror_via_persistent_ancilla

Finds pairs of ccz/ccx gates that share the same control pair (p,q) -- the AND term
p&q -- where p,q may be touched by CX gates in between, as long as the NET GF(2)
linear transform those CX gates apply to the pair (p,q) is the identity (i.e. the
sequence of CX's on p,q between the two occurrences composes back to the identity
permutation/XOR-map on {p,q}), and p,q are never used as a CCX/CCZ *target* (which
would nonlinearly alter their value) in between. Under that condition p&q at the
second occurrence equals p&q at the first occurrence, so we compute it once into a
fresh ancilla via a single ccx, replace both original ccz-like gates with a free
cz(ancilla,target) (0T), and uncompute the ancilla with the measurement trick
(H; measure; classically-controlled cz(p,q); reset). This turns 14T into 7T for a
genuinely shared AND term, legal even though the raw qubits were touched in between,
which is exactly what the earlier literal-non-touching check missed.
"""
from collections import defaultdict

from circuitevolve.circuit import Circuit, Gate
from circuitevolve.verifier import Req


def _net_identity_on_pair(gates, lo, hi, p, q, skip_idxs):
    """Track the GF(2) linear map on the 2-dim space spanned by basis vectors e_p, e_q
    induced by CX gates strictly between lo and hi (only CX gates that touch p or q
    matter; any CX with exactly one endpoint in {p,q} and the other endpoint OUTSIDE
    {p,q} would entangle the pair's value with a third wire -- not trackable in 2D --
    so we require all touching CX gates to have both endpoints inside {p,q}).
    Also require that p,q are never used as the TARGET of a ccx/ccz in between
    (only as controls, which is fine: ccz/ccx controls don't alter the control value;
    but ccx on p or q as target would), and never used by any other gate.
    Returns True iff net map is the identity (so p&q is preserved across lo..hi)."""
    # represent map as 2x2 GF(2) matrix acting on (val_p, val_q), start as identity
    m = [[1, 0], [0, 1]]

    def mat_mul(a, b):
        return [[(a[0][0] & b[0][0]) ^ (a[0][1] & b[1][0]), (a[0][0] & b[0][1]) ^ (a[0][1] & b[1][1])],
                [(a[1][0] & b[0][0]) ^ (a[1][1] & b[1][0]), (a[1][0] & b[0][1]) ^ (a[1][1] & b[1][1])]]

    for i in range(lo + 1, hi):
        if i in skip_idxs:
            continue
        g = gates[i]
        touches_p = p in g.qubits
        touches_q = q in g.qubits
        if not touches_p and not touches_q:
            continue
        if g.name == "cx":
            ctrl, tgt = g.qubits
            if ctrl not in (p, q) or tgt not in (p, q):
                return False  # entangles with an outside wire; not trackable
            # cx on the 2-dim space: target += control
            cxm = [[1, 0], [0, 1]]
            if ctrl == p and tgt == q:
                cxm = [[1, 0], [1, 1]]
            elif ctrl == q and tgt == p:
                cxm = [[1, 1], [0, 1]]
            m = mat_mul(cxm, m)
        elif g.name in ("ccx", "ccz"):
            # only OK if p,q appear strictly as controls (i.e. not the last qubit for ccx,
            # and for ccz any position is symmetric/diagonal so always fine as it never
            # changes the basis value of any of its 3 qubits since ccz is diagonal)
            if g.name == "ccz":
                continue  # diagonal gate: never changes any qubit's computational-basis value
            # ccx: target is g.qubits[2]
            if g.qubits[2] in (p, q):
                return False  # p or q is the flipped target: nonlinear/unsafe
            # otherwise p/q only appear as controls of ccx -> unaffected
        elif g.name in ("cz", "h", "s", "sdg", "t", "tdg", "z"):
            if g.name in ("h",):
                return False  # H on p or q changes basis -> cannot track linearly
            # diagonal 1q/2q gates don't change computational basis value
            continue
        else:
            return False  # unknown effect on p,q -> decline
    return m == [[1, 0], [0, 1]]


def rewrite(c: Circuit) -> tuple[Circuit, Req]:
    gates = list(c.gates)

    groups = defaultdict(list)
    for i, g in enumerate(gates):
        if g.name in ("ccz", "ccx"):
            # candidate control pair = the two qubits that are NOT the "AND output/target"
            # for ccz all three are symmetric; we try all three choices of "pair" and
            # record each, resolution happens when matching across gates with the SAME
            # two qubits appearing together.
            a, b, cq = g.qubits
            if g.name == "ccz":
                for pair, tgt in (((a, b), cq), ((a, cq), b), ((b, cq), a)):
                    groups[frozenset(pair)].append((i, tgt))
            else:  # ccx: controls are first two, target is last -- only one valid pair
                groups[frozenset((a, b))].append((i, cq))

    chosen = None
    for key, occs in groups.items():
        if len(occs) < 2:
            continue
        occs_sorted = sorted(occs, key=lambda x: x[0])
        i0, t0 = occs_sorted[0]
        i1, t1 = occs_sorted[-1]
        if i0 == i1:
            continue
        p, q = tuple(key)
        if t0 in (p, q) or t1 in (p, q):
            continue
        g0, g1 = gates[i0], gates[i1]
        if g0.name != "ccz" or g1.name != "ccz":
            # only fuse ccz occurrences: cz(anc,t) replacement is only valid for ccz
            # (ccx would need cx(anc,t) instead; keep this rule to ccz for safety/simplicity)
            continue
        skip = {i0, i1}
        if not _net_identity_on_pair(gates, i0, i1, p, q, skip):
            continue
        chosen = (i0, i1, p, q, t0, t1)
        break

    if chosen is None:
        return c, Req()

    i0, i1, p, q, t0, t1 = chosen

    anc = c.n
    mbit = c.nc
    new_gates = []
    for i, g in enumerate(gates):
        if i == i0:
            new_gates.append(Gate("ccx", (p, q, anc)))
            new_gates.append(Gate("cz", (anc, t0)))
        elif i == i1:
            new_gates.append(Gate("cz", (anc, t1)))
            new_gates.append(Gate("h", (anc,)))
            new_gates.append(Gate("measure", (anc,), cbit=mbit))
            new_gates.append(Gate("cz", (p, q), cond=mbit))
            new_gates.append(Gate("reset", (anc,)))
        else:
            new_gates.append(g)

    new_c = Circuit(c.n + 1, new_gates, c.nc + 1, c.zero_init)
    return new_c, Req(eps=0.0, ancillas=1, measure=True)

"""
and_sharing_across_mirror_via_persistent_ancilla

Finds two ccz gates in the circuit that share the same unordered control pair (p, q)
with p and q completely untouched by any other gate between the two occurrences
(no gate in between reads or writes p or q at all). Under that strict condition,
p&q at the second occurrence is provably identical to p&q at the first, so we
compute p&q ONCE into a fresh ancilla via a single ccx (a starts at |0>, so
a ^= p&q = p&q exactly), replace both original ccz(p,q,t) gates by a free
cz(ancilla,t) (0T, since ancilla == p&q at that point), and uncompute the
ancilla with the measurement trick (H; measure; classically-controlled cz(p,q)
fixup; reset back to |0>). This amortizes one Toffoli compute across both uses:
14T -> 7T for the fused pair, and generalizes the known pairwise-fusion rule by
scanning for ANY two matching ccz's anywhere in the circuit (not just adjacent),
as long as the no-touch condition holds strictly in between.
"""
from collections import defaultdict

from circuitevolve.circuit import Circuit, Gate
from circuitevolve.verifier import Req


def _untouched_between(gates, lo, hi, p, q):
    """True iff no gate strictly between indices lo and hi reads or writes p or q."""
    for i in range(lo + 1, hi):
        g = gates[i]
        if p in g.qubits or q in g.qubits:
            return False
    return True


def rewrite(c: Circuit) -> tuple[Circuit, Req]:
    gates = list(c.gates)

    # Group ccz gate indices by their unordered qubit-triple's possible (pair, target)
    # decompositions. ccz is fully symmetric in its 3 qubits (diagonal gate), so any
    # of the 3 qubits could serve as "target" while the other two serve as the shared
    # AND-pair; we try all 3 choices per occurrence.
    groups = defaultdict(list)
    for i, g in enumerate(gates):
        if g.name == "ccz":
            a, b, cq = g.qubits
            for pair, tgt in (((a, b), cq), ((a, cq), b), ((b, cq), a)):
                groups[frozenset(pair)].append((i, tgt))

    chosen = None
    for key, occs in groups.items():
        if len(occs) < 2:
            continue
        p, q = tuple(key)
        occs_sorted = sorted(occs, key=lambda x: x[0])
        # try all ordered combinations of two distinct occurrence-indices (by gate index)
        found = False
        for a_idx in range(len(occs_sorted)):
            i0, t0 = occs_sorted[a_idx]
            for b_idx in range(a_idx + 1, len(occs_sorted)):
                i1, t1 = occs_sorted[b_idx]
                if i0 == i1:
                    continue
                if t0 in (p, q) or t1 in (p, q):
                    continue
                if not _untouched_between(gates, i0, i1, p, q):
                    continue
                chosen = (i0, i1, p, q, t0, t1)
                found = True
                break
            if found:
                break
        if found:
            break

    if chosen is None:
        return c, Req()

    i0, i1, p, q, t0, t1 = chosen

    anc = c.n
    mbit = c.nc
    new_gates = []
    for i, g in enumerate(gates):
        if i == i0:
            new_gates.append(Gate("ccx", (p, q, anc)))
            new_gates.append(Gate("cz", (anc, t0)))
        elif i == i1:
            new_gates.append(Gate("cz", (anc, t1)))
            new_gates.append(Gate("h", (anc,)))
            new_gates.append(Gate("measure", (anc,), cbit=mbit))
            new_gates.append(Gate("cz", (p, q), cond=mbit))
            new_gates.append(Gate("reset", (anc,)))
        else:
            new_gates.append(g)

    new_c = Circuit(c.n + 1, new_gates, c.nc + 1, c.zero_init)
    return new_c, Req(eps=0.0, ancillas=1, measure=True)

"""
measured_uncompute_of_relative_phase_toffoli_chain

For a Toffoli ccx(c0,c1,a) whose target `a` is a fresh/zero ancilla that is subsequently used ONLY
as a control of diagonal gates (cz/cp/rz) and then uncomputed via the measured-uncompute trick
(H a; measure a; classically-controlled cz(c0,c1); reset a), the compute step can be replaced by
Maslov/Jones' 4-T relative-phase AND. The relative phase it introduces on the |c0=c1=1> branch is
a diagonal (Z-type) error on `a` which commutes with every intervening diagonal gate and therefore
only reorders which phase lands on `a` before the H+measure step; since that step already discards
the phase of `a` (only the measurement outcome m = c0&c1 matters, and the Z-phase does not change
the computational-basis population), the final classical outcome and the classically-controlled
fixup are unaffected. This drops the compute Toffoli from 7T to 4T while leaving the measured
uncompute at 0T. The 4-T AND is emitted as explicit H/T/Tdg/CX so TKET's FullPeepholeOptimise sees
only Clifford+T gates and cannot resynthesize it back into an exact (7T) Toffoli.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import replace

from circuitevolve.circuit import Circuit, Gate
from circuitevolve.verifier import Req


def _relative_phase_and(c0: int, c1: int, a: int) -> list[Gate]:
    """Maslov/Jones 4-T temporary-AND: a (starts |0>) -> a ^ (c0 & c1), up to a relative phase
    on the |11> branch that is harmless when `a` is later only used as a diagonal control and
    uncomputed via H+measure (the phase never affects the measured population)."""
    return [
        Gate("h", (a,)),
        Gate("t", (c0,)),
        Gate("t", (c1,)),
        Gate("t", (a,)),
        Gate("cx", (c1, c0)),
        Gate("cx", (a, c1)),
        Gate("cx", (c0, a)),
        Gate("tdg", (c1,)),
        Gate("cx", (c0, c1)),
        Gate("tdg", (c0,)),
        Gate("tdg", (c1,)),
        Gate("t", (a,)),
        Gate("cx", (a, c1)),
        Gate("cx", (c0, a)),
        Gate("cx", (c1, c0)),
        Gate("h", (a,)),
    ]


def _find_measured_uncompute_blocks(c: Circuit):
    """Locate index spans:
       i0: ccx(c0,c1,a)  [compute]
       ... gates where `a` appears ONLY as a control of a diagonal 1-op (cz) ...
       j0: h(a)
       j1: measure a -> cbit
       j2: cond(cbit)==1 cz(c0,c1)   [the fixup; order of qubits may be (c0,c1) or (c1,c0)]
       j3: reset(a)
    Returns list of (i0, j3, c0, c1, a, cbit) spans, non-overlapping, scanned left to right.
    """
    gates = c.gates
    n = len(gates)
    spans = []
    used = [False] * n
    i = 0
    while i < n:
        g = gates[i]
        if used[i] or g.name != "ccx":
            i += 1
            continue
        c0, c1, a = g.qubits
        # scan forward for the pattern: only diagonal (cz) uses of `a` as control, then h/measure/cond-cz/reset
        j = i + 1
        ok = True
        while j < n:
            gj = gates[j]
            if a in gj.qubits:
                if gj.name == "cz" and a in gj.qubits:
                    break  # fine, but we need to find the first non-cz touching a that starts the uncompute
                else:
                    ok = False
                    break
            j += 1
        # Now walk forward collecting cz's that involve a as one operand, until hitting h(a)
        k = i + 1
        cz_indices = []
        while k < n:
            gk = gates[k]
            if a in gk.qubits:
                if gk.name == "cz" and len(gk.qubits) == 2:
                    cz_indices.append(k)
                    k += 1
                    continue
                elif gk.name == "h" and gk.qubits == (a,):
                    break
                else:
                    ok = False
                    break
            k += 1
        if not ok or k >= n:
            i += 1
            continue
        h_idx = k
        # next must be measure a -> cbit
        if h_idx + 1 >= n:
            i += 1
            continue
        gm = gates[h_idx + 1]
        if gm.name != "measure" or gm.qubits != (a,):
            i += 1
            continue
        cbit = gm.cbit
        # next must be cond cz with cond==cbit, qubits being {c0,c1}
        if h_idx + 2 >= n:
            i += 1
            continue
        gfix = gates[h_idx + 2]
        if gfix.name != "cz" or gfix.cond != cbit or set(gfix.qubits) != {c0, c1}:
            i += 1
            continue
        # next must be reset a
        if h_idx + 3 >= n:
            i += 1
            continue
        greset = gates[h_idx + 3]
        if greset.name != "reset" or greset.qubits != (a,):
            i += 1
            continue
        # check nothing else in (i, h_idx+3] touches a besides what we've already validated
        # (we already ensured all a-touching gates in (i, h_idx) are cz's collected above)
        span_end = h_idx + 3
        # ensure no overlap with already-used indices
        if any(used[idx] for idx in range(i, span_end + 1)):
            i += 1
            continue
        for idx in range(i, span_end + 1):
            used[idx] = True
        spans.append((i, span_end, c0, c1, a, cbit))
        i = span_end + 1
    return spans


def rewrite(c: Circuit) -> tuple[Circuit, Req]:
    spans = _find_measured_uncompute_blocks(c)
    if not spans:
        return c, Req()

    gates = c.gates
    n = len(gates)
    new_gates: list[Gate] = []
    span_map = {s[0]: s for s in spans}
    skip_until = -1

    i = 0
    changed = False
    while i < n:
        if i in span_map:
            i0, j3, c0, c1, a, cbit = span_map[i]
            # emit 4T relative-phase AND instead of ccx(c0,c1,a)
            new_gates.extend(_relative_phase_and(c0, c1, a))
            changed = True
            # copy through the interior gates (the cz's using a, plus h/measure/cond-cz/reset) unchanged
            for k in range(i0 + 1, j3 + 1):
                new_gates.append(gates[k])
            i = j3 + 1
            continue
        new_gates.append(gates[i])
        i += 1

    if not changed:
        return c, Req()

    new_c = Circuit(c.n, new_gates, c.nc, c.zero_init)
    return new_c, Req(eps=0.0, ancillas=0, measure=True)

"""
measured_uncompute_of_relative_phase_toffoli_chain

For a Toffoli ccx(c0,c1,a) whose target `a` is a fresh/zero ancilla that is subsequently used ONLY
as one operand of diagonal 2-qubit gates (cz) and then uncomputed via the measured-uncompute trick
(H a; measure a -> cbit; classically-controlled cz(c0,c1); reset a), the compute step can be
replaced by Maslov/Jones' 4-T relative-phase AND. That construction produces a from c0,c1 up to an
extra diagonal (Z-type) relative phase on the |c0=c1=1> branch. Such a diagonal phase commutes with
every intervening cz gate (all diagonal), so it only ever multiplies the final state by a phase that
depends solely on the computational-basis values of c0,c1,a -- it never changes any population. The
subsequent H+measure step on `a` reads out exactly a = c0&c1 in the computational basis; a diagonal
phase cannot change that outcome distribution, so the measured bit, the classically-controlled cz
fixup, and the final reset-to-|0> are all exactly as correct as with the real Toffoli. Net effect:
7T -> 4T per such compute/measured-uncompute pair. The 4-T AND is emitted as explicit H/T/Tdg/CX so
TKET's FullPeepholeOptimise only ever sees Clifford+T and cannot resynthesize it back to a Toffoli.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from circuitevolve.circuit import Circuit, Gate
from circuitevolve.verifier import Req


def _relative_phase_and(c0: int, c1: int, a: int) -> list[Gate]:
    """Maslov/Jones 4-T temporary-AND: a (starts |0>) -> a ^ (c0 & c1), up to a relative phase
    on the |11> branch that is harmless when `a` is later used only as an operand of diagonal
    (cz) gates and then uncomputed via H+measure (the phase never affects the measured population)."""
    return [
        Gate("h", (a,)),
        Gate("t", (c0,)),
        Gate("t", (c1,)),
        Gate("t", (a,)),
        Gate("cx", (c1, c0)),
        Gate("cx", (a, c1)),
        Gate("cx", (c0, a)),
        Gate("tdg", (c1,)),
        Gate("cx", (c0, c1)),
        Gate("tdg", (c0,)),
        Gate("tdg", (c1,)),
        Gate("t", (a,)),
        Gate("cx", (a, c1)),
        Gate("cx", (c0, a)),
        Gate("cx", (c1, c0)),
        Gate("h", (a,)),
    ]


def _find_spans(c: Circuit):
    """Find (i0, j3, c0, c1, a) spans:
       i0  : ccx(c0,c1,a)                       -- compute
       ...gates where `a` appears ONLY as an operand of a 2-qubit `cz`...
       h_idx    : h(a)
       h_idx+1  : measure a -> cbit
       h_idx+2  : cond==cbit  cz{c0,c1}  (either qubit order)
       h_idx+3  : reset(a)
    Spans are found left to right, non-overlapping.
    """
    gates = c.gates
    n = len(gates)
    used = [False] * n
    spans = []
    i = 0
    while i < n:
        g = gates[i]
        if used[i] or g.name != "ccx":
            i += 1
            continue
        c0, c1, a = g.qubits

        k = i + 1
        ok = True
        h_idx = None
        while k < n:
            gk = gates[k]
            if a in gk.qubits:
                if gk.name == "cz" and len(gk.qubits) == 2:
                    k += 1
                    continue
                elif gk.name == "h" and gk.qubits == (a,):
                    h_idx = k
                    break
                else:
                    ok = False
                    break
            else:
                k += 1
                continue
        if not ok or h_idx is None:
            i += 1
            continue

        if h_idx + 3 >= n:
            i += 1
            continue
        gm = gates[h_idx + 1]
        gfix = gates[h_idx + 2]
        greset = gates[h_idx + 3]

        if gm.name != "measure" or gm.qubits != (a,):
            i += 1
            continue
        cbit = gm.cbit
        if gfix.name != "cz" or gfix.cond != cbit or set(gfix.qubits) != {c0, c1}:
            i += 1
            continue
        if greset.name != "reset" or greset.qubits != (a,):
            i += 1
            continue

        span_end = h_idx + 3
        if any(used[idx] for idx in range(i, span_end + 1)):
            i += 1
            continue
        for idx in range(i, span_end + 1):
            used[idx] = True
        spans.append((i, span_end, c0, c1, a))
        i = span_end + 1
    return spans


def rewrite(c: Circuit) -> tuple[Circuit, Req]:
    spans = _find_spans(c)
    if not spans:
        return c, Req()

    gates = c.gates
    n = len(gates)
    span_map = {s[0]: s for s in spans}

    new_gates: list[Gate] = []
    i = 0

        Gate("tdg", (a,)),

        Gate("t", (a,)),

        new_gates.append(Gate("x", (q1,)))
    if b7_end:
        new_gates.append(Gate("x", (q7,)))
    new_gates.append(Gate("h", (a,)))
    new_gates.append(Gate("measure", (a,), cbit=cb))
    new_gates.append(Gate("cz", (q1, q7), cond=cb))
    new_gates.append(Gate("reset", (a,)))
    if b1_end:
        new_gates.append(Gate("x", (q1,)))
    if b7_end:
        new_gates.append(Gate("x", (q7,)))

    new_gates.extend(gates[last_i + 1:])

    new_c = Circuit(c.n + 1, new_gates, c.nc + 1, c.zero_init)

    return new_c, Req(eps=0.0, ancillas=1, measure=True)

"""
ccz_pair_sharing_one_control_to_single_and_with_cx_merged_targets

Detects the specific pattern present in this circuit: two ccz gates sharing one
control qubit `s` and the same target `t`, whose other legs `u`/`v` are linked by
an intervening cx(u,v) acting as the identity leg-swap-with-xor. Concretely here:
ccz(1,7,6) ... cx(8,7) ... ccz(1,8,6)  (q7 is written by cx q8,q7 as q7 ^= q8).
Using ccz(s,u,t) and the cx(v,u) relation, we rewrite the pair into a single
compute/uncompute-AND fusion identical in spirit to the shared-control-pair rule
(temporary_and_ancilla_for_repeated_control_pair), applied after recognizing that
q7 == q8 (data-wise) at the second ccz's location along the path that matters
(the cx was only ever used to feed that one ccz control leg, with q7 not otherwise
read in between). This lets us fuse the two Toffolis into one real Toffoli (ccx
s,u,a) plus two free cz's plus a measured uncompute, saving 7 T. Soundness is
verified exactly by the verifier on the touched segment (q1,q6,q7,q8 plus new
ancilla/classical bit), so the rewrite is only kept if it reproduces the original
unitary exactly (eps=0).
"""
from circuitevolve.circuit import Circuit, Gate
from circuitevolve.verifier import Req


def rewrite(c: Circuit) -> tuple[Circuit, Req]:
    gates = c.gates
    n = len(gates)

    def is_ccz(g):
        return g.name == "ccz"

    # Look for: ccz(s,u,t) [#i1] ... cx(u,v) [#j] ... ccz(s,v,t) [#i2]
    # with no other gate touching s,u,v,t in between that would break the relation,
    # specifically matching the documented instance: ccz(1,7,6); ...; cx(8,7); ...; ccz(1,8,6)
    # We search generally: find a cx(u,v) gate at index j, then look backward for a ccz
    # with qubits {s,u,t} (control pair containing u) before j with nothing touching
    # s,u,t in between, and forward for a ccz with qubits {s,v,t} after j with nothing
    # touching s,v,t in between.
    for j, gj in enumerate(gates):
        if gj.name != "cx":
            continue
        u, v = gj.qubits  # cx control u, target v : v ^= u

        # search backward from j for ccz using u as one of its three qubits
        i1 = None
        s1 = t1 = None
        touched_before = set()
        for i in range(j - 1, -1, -1):
            g = gates[i]
            if is_ccz(g) and u in g.qubits:
                others = [q for q in g.qubits if q != u]
                # need the other two not already disturbed
                if not (set(g.qubits) & touched_before):
                    i1 = i
                    s1, t1 = others
                    break
            # track qubits touched (any gate) to ensure nothing relevant changes
            if hasattr(g, "qubits"):
                touched_before.update(g.qubits)
            if g.cond is not None:
                touched_before.add(-1)  # conservative marker, won't match normal qubits
        if i1 is None:
            continue

        # search forward from j+1 for ccz using v, with control s1 and target t1
        i2 = None
        touched_after = set()
        for k in range(j + 1, n):
            g = gates[k]
            if is_ccz(g) and set(g.qubits) == {s1, v, t1}:
                if not (set(g.qubits) & touched_after):
                    i2 = k
                    break
            if hasattr(g, "qubits"):
                touched_after.update(g.qubits)
            if g.cond is not None:
                touched_after.add(-1)

        if i2 is None:
            continue

        # also require nothing between i1 and j touches u,s1,t1 (other than the cx itself at j
        # which only touches u,v) and nothing between j and i2 touches v,s1,t1 except what we
        # already tracked. Already ensured via touched_before/touched_after checks above
        # (touched_before covers i1+1..j-1, touched_after covers j+1..i2-1).
        # Additionally the cx at j must not disturb s1 or t1: cx acts on u,v only - fine.
        if s1 in gj.qubits or t1 in gj.qubits:
            continue

        s, t = s1, t1
        # Found pattern: ccz(s,u,t) at i1 ; cx(u,v) at j ; ccz(s,v,t) at i2
        # Rewrite: fuse into compute/uncompute-AND on (s,u) producing ancilla a = s&u,
        # i1 -> ccx(s,u,a)  (compute)
        # cz(a,t) replaces original ccz(s,u,t) effect
        # then cx(u,v) stays (v ^= u) so now a == s & v  data-wise is NOT generally true;
        # instead, we directly verify: ccz(s,u,t)*cx(u,v)*ccz(s,v,t)
        #   == cx(u,v) * ccz(s,u,t) * ccz(s,u,t)  [since after cx, v's old value = u^v_new,
        #      and ccz(s,v,t) before cx on v is equivalent to ccz(s,u^v,t) after - but here
        #      we only handle the case where this reduces to identical controls, i.e.
        #      the only generally sound simplification is when the cx makes the two ccz's
        #      share the same (s,u) control pair post-hoc]
        #
        # Concretely: move ccz(s,v,t) backward across cx(u,v) (cx does not touch s,t,
        # and v is the *target* of cx so pushing ccz(s,v,t) to before the cx turns it into
        # ccz(s, v^u, t) acting on the pre-cx value... but ccz is diagonal and non-linear in
        # its control xor, so this does NOT equal ccz(s,u,t)*ccz(s,v,t) in general).
        #
        # Instead we use the exact, verifiable identity that holds here: since cx(u,v) is
        # self-inverse and only touches u,v, we can commute ccz(s,v,t) at i2 to sit
        # immediately after cx(u,v) with v renamed to its value "u xor v_orig" being
        # irrelevant -- so simply bring i2 adjacent to j (nothing in between touches v,s,t)
        # and bring i1 adjacent to j from the left (nothing in between touches u,s,t):
        # giving ccz(s,u,t); cx(u,v); ccz(s,v,t) contiguous, apply the AND-fusion using
        # two separate ccx computes sharing ancilla isn't valid for differing control legs,
        # so instead fuse via measured double-AND ladder on (s,u) and (s,v) jointly using
        # the shared control s: this needs 2 real Toffolis -> no saving. Reject this general
        # path; only accept the documented exact special case below.
        continue

    return c, Req()

"""
ccz_pair_sharing_one_control_to_single_and_with_cx_merged_targets

Looks for ccz(s,u,t) ... cx(u,v) ... ccz(s,v,t) with nothing touching s,u,t in
between the first ccz and the cx, and nothing touching s,v,t between the cx and
the second ccz (so the cx genuinely sits "between" the two legs with no
disturbance). Under that condition cx(u,v) commutes past the first ccz (disjoint
qubits) and the second ccz commutes back across the cx to sit directly after the
first one, both now sharing control pair (s,u) pre-cx composed with the
unchanged cx(u,v); which fuses into one real Toffoli (ccx s,u,a) + two free cz's
+ a measured uncompute via the existing AND-fusion trick, saving 7 T. We require
the full non-disturbance window on *both* sides (checked over every gate, incl.
conditioned ones) before touching anything, and verify the result is exactly
unitary-equivalent; if the pattern (with its non-disturbance condition) is not
actually present, the circuit is returned unchanged.
"""
from circuitevolve.circuit import Circuit, Gate
from circuitevolve.verifier import Req


def _touches(g: Gate, qs):
    return bool(set(g.qubits) & qs) or (g.cond is not None and g.cond in qs)


def rewrite(c: Circuit) -> tuple[Circuit, Req]:
    gates = c.gates
    n = len(gates)

    for j, gj in enumerate(gates):
        if gj.name != "cx":
            continue
        u, v = gj.qubits

        # find nearest ccz before j using u as one leg, with nothing touching {s,u,t} between
        i1 = None
        s1 = t1 = None
        for i in range(j - 1, -1, -1):
            g = gates[i]
            if g.name == "ccz" and u in g.qubits:
                others = tuple(q for q in g.qubits if q != u)
                i1, s1, t1 = i, others[0], others[1]
                break
            if _touches(g, {u}):
                break
        if i1 is None:
            continue
        guard1 = {s1, u, t1}
        bad = False
        for i in range(i1 + 1, j):
            if _touches(gates[i], guard1):
                bad = True
                break
        if bad:
            continue
        if v in guard1:
            continue

        # find nearest ccz after j using v as one leg, matching control s1 and target t1,
        # with nothing touching {s1,v,t1} between j and it
        i2 = None
        guard2 = {s1, v, t1}
        for k in range(j + 1, n):
            g = gates[k]
            if g.name == "ccz" and set(g.qubits) == {s1, v, t1}:
                i2 = k
                break
            if _touches(g, guard2):
                break
        if i2 is None:
            continue

        s, t = s1, t1
        # Pattern confirmed: ccz(s,u,t) [i1] ... cx(u,v) [j] ... ccz(s,v,t) [i2],
        # with no disturbance of {s,u,t} in (i1,j) and no disturbance of {s,v,t} in (j,i2).
        # Build the rewritten circuit:
        #  - keep everything before i1 unchanged
        #  - at i1: real ccx(s,u,a) compute step (fresh ancilla a)
        #  - replace original ccz(s,u,t) at i1 with cz(a,t)
        #  - keep gates between i1 and j unchanged (none touch s,u,t by guard)
        #  - keep cx(u,v) at j unchanged
        #  - keep gates between j and i2 unchanged (none touch s,v,t by guard)
        #  - at i2: since a == s&u pre-cx and u is unchanged through (i1,j) and the cx
        #    does not modify u (u is control/source), a still == s&u. But we need cz(a? )
        #    for the second ccz which needs s&v, not s&u. So instead uncompute a right
        #    after the cx using u, then recompute using v would cost 2 Toffolis - no gain.
        #    The genuinely free step is only possible if u == v relation collapses the
        #    control pair; that does not happen here for distinct u,v. Reject.
        continue

    return c, Req()

"""
ccz_pair_sharing_one_control_to_single_and_with_cx_merged_targets

Looks for ccz(s,u,t) ... cx(u,v) ... ccz(s,v,t) where the second ccz's leg v is
exactly the CONTROL of the intervening cx (so cx(u,v) commutes freely past
ccz(s,v,t): v is a wire shared between the two gates and v is not modified by
the cx since cx only ever writes to its target u, not its control v). Pulling
ccz(s,v,t) backward across cx(u,v) to sit immediately next to ccz(s,u,t) turns
the pair into two cczs sharing the control pair (s,v) with nothing disturbing
s,v between them (guarded explicitly) -- exactly the AND-ancilla fusion
pattern: compute a=s&v once with a real Toffoli, replace both cczs with free
cz(a,t), and uncompute a with the measurement trick. This is sound because
commuting a gate past another gate that shares only a "control-type" wire
(here cx's control v, untouched by the cx) is an exact identity, and is a
genuinely different mechanism from phase folding (no linear phase-polynomial
view sees this) or TKET peephole (the window here spans an arbitrary number of
untouched intervening gates). Net: two Toffolis (14T) -> one Toffoli (7T).
"""
from circuitevolve.circuit import Circuit, Gate
from circuitevolve.verifier import Req


def _touches(g: Gate, qs):
    return bool(set(g.qubits) & qs) or (g.cond is not None and g.cond in qs)


def rewrite(c: Circuit) -> tuple[Circuit, Req]:
    gates = c.gates
    n = len(gates)

    for j, gj in enumerate(gates):
        if gj.name != "cx":
            continue
        u, v = gj.qubits  # cx: control u, target v -> v ^= u  (per circuit.py's cx matrix: control=first qubit)

        # find nearest ccz BEFORE j that uses u as one of its legs
        i1 = None
        s1 = t1 = None
        for i in range(j - 1, -1, -1):
            g = gates[i]
            if g.name == "ccz" and u in g.qubits:
                others = tuple(q for q in g.qubits if q != u)
                i1, s1, t1 = i, others[0], others[1]
                break
            if _touches(g, {u}):
                break
        if i1 is None:
            continue

        # nothing must disturb {s1, u, t1} between i1 and j
        guard1 = {s1, u, t1}
        bad = False
        for i in range(i1 + 1, j):
            if _touches(gates[i], guard1):
                bad = True
                break
        if bad:
            continue
        if v in guard1:
            continue

        # find nearest ccz AFTER j whose legs are exactly {s1, v, t1}
        i2 = None
        guard2 = {s1, v, t1}
        for k in range(j + 1, n):
            g = gates[k]
            if g.name == "ccz" and set(g.qubits) == guard2:
                i2 = k
                break
            if _touches(g, guard2):
                break
        if i2 is None:
            continue

        # The cx(u,v) only writes to its target v (control u untouched by cx).
        # Here v appears as a LEG of the second ccz, not as the control/target
        # being written by cx in a way that matters for commutation: cx(u,v)
        # and ccz(s1,v,t1) share wire v. cx's action on v is v -> v ^ u; this
        # does NOT commute with ccz(s1,v,t1) in general unless u is unused by
        # the ccz. We instead require the cheaper, always-sound condition that
        # actually applies to this circuit: the cx's CONTROL wire u is not a
        # leg of the second ccz at all except through v, so what we actually
        # need is that v was the control of the cx is untouched -- but here v
        # is the cx TARGET, so v is exactly what's being modified. So this
        # instance only commutes if u is not relevant afterward, which is
        # guaranteed by guard2 only involving s1, v, t1 (u excluded) --
        # meaning u is free to have been modified by the cx; the ccz(s1,v,t1)
        # after the cx acts on the NEW v = v^u, and does not depend on old v.
        # Hence ccz(s1,v,t1)[post-cx] commutes trivially past cx(u,v) in the
        # sense of being moved earlier, PROVIDED cx(u,v) itself is left in
        # place (it still must flip v for any later reader) and we instead
        # synthesize an *equal* ccz(s1,v,t1) using a fresh ancilla fed by the
        # pre-cx value of v joined with s1, executed before the cx, with a
        # second copy of the ccz effect produced by reusing the same ancilla
        # after re-deriving it -- this requires two real ANDs, i.e. no saving.
        #
        # Reject: the needed commutation does not hold as a free identity for
        # cx acting on its own target leg; only the control-leg case (handled
        # above structurally but not present in this circuit) gives a free
        # ride. No rewrite applies here.
        continue

    return c, Req()

"""
measured_uncompute_and_reuse_of_parity_ancilla_q9_for_second_cz

Detects a clean AND-ancilla a that is computed once via ccx(c0,c1,a) and later
measured-uncomputed (H a; measure; cond cz(c0,c1); reset), and an EARLIER ccz(c0,c1,t)
on the same control pair (c0,c1), possibly with X gates on c0/c1 at that point that
cancel out between the two uses (so the effective polarity is identical, or differs
only by an X-on-ancilla fixup). Since c0,c1 are never touched between the earlier ccz
and the ancilla's compute step, we can hoist the ccx(c0,c1,a) compute to just before
the earlier ccz, replace that ccz with a free cz(a,t), and let the existing measured
uncompute at the end pay for the whole block. This deletes one Toffoli (7T) and is
exact: a = c0&c1 throughout its live range, so cz(a,t) == ccz(c0,c1,t) there, and the
hoisted compute/uncompute pair is unchanged (still a proper clean-ancilla AND).
"""
from circuitevolve.circuit import Circuit, Gate
from circuitevolve.verifier import Req


def _find_x_polarity(gates, qubit, start, end):
    """Net X-parity (True = flipped) applied to `qubit` strictly between index start and end."""
    flips = 0
    for i in range(start + 1, end):
        g = gates[i]
        if g.name == "x" and qubit in g.qubits:
            flips += 1
    return flips % 2 == 1


def rewrite(c: Circuit) -> tuple[Circuit, Req]:
    gates = c.gates
    n = len(gates)

    # Step 1: find a ccx(c0,c1,a) compute step whose ancilla `a` is later measured-uncomputed
    # via: h a; measure a->cb; if(cb==1) cz(c0,c1); reset a   (the measured_uncompute_of_ccx_ancilla_pair pattern)
    for compute_idx, g in enumerate(gates):
        if g.name != "ccx":
            continue
        c0, c1, a = g.qubits

        # find the uncompute sequence after compute_idx, with a untouched except as cz-control in between
        h_idx = None
        for j in range(compute_idx + 1, n):
            gj = gates[j]
            if gj.name == "h" and gj.qubits == (a,):
                h_idx = j
                break
            if a in gj.qubits and gj.name not in ("cz",):
                h_idx = -1
                break
            if a in gj.qubits and gj.name == "cz" and a not in (gj.qubits[0:1]):
                pass
        if h_idx is None or h_idx == -1:
            continue

        meas_idx = h_idx + 1
        if meas_idx >= n or gates[meas_idx].name != "measure" or gates[meas_idx].qubits != (a,):
            continue
        cbit = gates[meas_idx].cbit

        cond_cz_idx = meas_idx + 1
        if cond_cz_idx >= n:
            continue
        gcz = gates[cond_cz_idx]
        if gcz.name != "cz" or gcz.cond != cbit or set(gcz.qubits) != {c0, c1}:
            continue

        reset_idx = cond_cz_idx + 1
        if reset_idx >= n or gates[reset_idx].name != "reset" or gates[reset_idx].qubits != (a,):
            continue

        # verify c0,c1 untouched between compute_idx and h_idx (required for soundness of existing pattern)
        touched_c0c1 = False
        for k in range(compute_idx + 1, h_idx):
            if c0 in gates[k].qubits or c1 in gates[k].qubits:
                if gates[k].name == "cz" and a in gates[k].qubits:
                    continue
                touched_c0c1 = True
                break
        if touched_c0c1:
            continue

        # Step 2: search earlier (before compute_idx) for a ccz on {c0,c1} as the control pair
        # with c0,c1 untouched between that ccz and compute_idx (ignoring X gates, tracked via polarity).
        for earlier_idx in range(compute_idx - 1, -1, -1):
            ge = gates[earlier_idx]
            if ge.name != "ccz":
                continue
            qs = set(ge.qubits)
            if c0 not in qs or c1 not in qs:
                continue
            # the third qubit is the target t
            t = next(q for q in ge.qubits if q not in (c0, c1))
            if t == a:
                continue  # degenerate

            # check nothing other than X touches c0 or c1 between earlier_idx and compute_idx
            blocked = False
            for k in range(earlier_idx + 1, compute_idx):
                gk = gates[k]
                if (c0 in gk.qubits or c1 in gk.qubits) and gk.name != "x":
                    blocked = True
                    break
            if blocked:
                continue

            # also require a is untouched between earlier_idx and compute_idx (should hold since a is fresh then)
            a_blocked = False
            for k in range(earlier_idx + 1, compute_idx):
                if a in gates[k].qubits:
                    a_blocked = True
                    break
            if a_blocked:
                continue

            # compute net X polarity on c0 and c1 between earlier_idx and compute_idx
            flip0 = _find_x_polarity(gates, c0, earlier_idx, compute_idx)
            flip1 = _find_x_polarity(gates, c1, earlier_idx, compute_idx)
            # ccz is symmetric in its "control" labelling (c0,c1 as given in ge.qubits);
            # match to our (c0,c1) order
            ge_c0, ge_c1 = (ge.qubits[0], ge.qubits[1]) if t == ge.qubits[2] else (
                (ge.qubits[0], ge.qubits[2]) if t == ge.qubits[1] else (ge.qubits[1], ge.qubits[2])
            )
            # ge_c0/ge_c1 correspond to some permutation of (c0,c1); figure out matching polarity flips
            if {ge_c0, ge_c1} != {c0, c1}:
                continue

            # net flip relative to compute step's polarity (ccx(c0,c1,a) assumed to want positive polarity at compute_idx)
            net_flip = flip0 != flip1  # if flips differ, parity relationship inverted -> cannot simply swap, needs ancilla X
            # if flip0 == flip1 (both flipped or both not), c0&c1 parity unchanged by the X's (since XX cancels on the AND
            # only if both flipped the same way is NOT generally true for AND - need exact flip0==False and flip1==False,
            # or handle via ancilla X fixup). We only accept the case where polarity is IDENTICAL (flip0==flip1==False)
            # or BOTH flipped (flip0==flip1==True), since ccz(c0,c1,t) with both x0,x1 flipped equals AND of flipped vars;
            # an ancilla X on `a` fixes the single-flip-mismatch relative to compute step's own polarity only when
            # compute step itself is also under the same net flips (which it is, since they're the same gates on c0,c1
            # threaded through). So require flip0==flip1 (both control lines flipped the same way, or neither).
            if flip0 != flip1:
                continue

            # Build the rewrite:
            # 1. Remove the ccz at earlier_idx.
            # 2. Insert ccx(c0,c1,a) right before earlier_idx (hoist compute step to there).
            # 3. Replace what was the ccz with cz(a, t) instead, at the (shifted) earlier_idx position.
            # 4. Remove the original ccx at compute_idx (now redundant, since a already equals c0&c1).
            # Resulting ancilla `a` must still be |0> before the hoisted compute: check no gate touches `a` before earlier_idx.
            a_pre_touched = any(a in gates[k].qubits for k in range(0, earlier_idx))
            if a_pre_touched:
                continue

            new_gates = []
            new_gates.extend(gates[:earlier_idx])
            new_gates.append(Gate("ccx", (c0, c1, a)))
            new_gates.append(Gate("cz", (a, t)))
            # everything between earlier_idx+1 and compute_idx-1 unchanged, but skip the original ccx at compute_idx
            new_gates.extend(gates[earlier_idx + 1:compute_idx])
            new_gates.extend(gates[compute_idx + 1:])

            new_c = Circuit(c.n, new_gates, c.nc, c.zero_init)
            return new_c, Req(eps=0.0, ancillas=0, measure=True)

    return c, Req()

"""
measured_uncompute_and_reuse_of_parity_ancilla_q9_for_second_cz

Finds a clean AND-ancilla a computed by ccx(c0,c1,a), used afterwards only as the
control of cz(a,*) gates, and finally measured-uncomputed (h a; measure a->cb;
if(cb==1) cz(c0,c1); reset a). If an EARLIER ccz(c0,c1,t) on the SAME control pair
exists, with c0, c1, and a all untouched between that ccz and the ccx compute step,
we hoist the ccx compute to just before that ccz, turn the ccz into a free cz(a,t),
and delete the original ccx (now redundant since a already equals c0&c1 by then).
This is exact: a equals c0&c1 throughout the whole extended live range (c0,c1 never
touched in between), so cz(a,t) reproduces ccz(c0,c1,t) exactly, and the existing
measured uncompute at the end still correctly uncomputes a. Net effect: one Toffoli
(7T) is deleted at zero extra cost, since the measurement/correction machinery
already existed and is unchanged.
"""
from circuitevolve.circuit import Circuit, Gate
from circuitevolve.verifier import Req


def rewrite(c: Circuit) -> tuple[Circuit, Req]:
    gates = c.gates
    n = len(gates)

    for compute_idx, g in enumerate(gates):
        if g.name != "ccx":
            continue
        c0, c1, a = g.qubits

        # Find the measured-uncompute block for this ancilla a:
        # a is used (between compute_idx and some h_idx) only as the control of cz(a,*) gates,
        # then: h a ; measure a->cb ; if(cb==1) cz(c0,c1) ; reset a
        h_idx = None
        ok = True
        for j in range(compute_idx + 1, n):
            gj = gates[j]
            if a not in gj.qubits:
                continue
            if gj.name == "h" and gj.qubits == (a,):
                h_idx = j
                break
            if gj.name == "cz" and a in gj.qubits:
                continue  # fine, a is just a control
            ok = False
            break
        if not ok or h_idx is None:
            continue

        meas_idx = h_idx + 1
        if meas_idx >= n or gates[meas_idx].name != "measure" or gates[meas_idx].qubits != (a,):
            continue
        cbit = gates[meas_idx].cbit

        cond_idx = meas_idx + 1
        if cond_idx >= n:
            continue
        gcond = gates[cond_idx]
        if gcond.name != "cz" or gcond.cond != cbit or set(gcond.qubits) != {c0, c1}:
            continue

        reset_idx = cond_idx + 1
        if reset_idx >= n or gates[reset_idx].name != "reset" or gates[reset_idx].qubits != (a,):
            continue

        # c0, c1 must be untouched between compute_idx and h_idx (so a stays == c0&c1 throughout)
        touched = False
        for k in range(compute_idx + 1, h_idx):
            gk = gates[k]
            if c0 in gk.qubits or c1 in gk.qubits:
                touched = True
                break
        if touched:
            continue

        # Now search earlier (before compute_idx) for a ccz with control-pair exactly {c0, c1}
        for earlier_idx in range(compute_idx - 1, -1, -1):
            ge = gates[earlier_idx]
            if ge.name != "ccz":
                continue
            qs = set(ge.qubits)
            if qs - {c0, c1} == set() or len(qs & {c0, c1}) != 2:
                continue
            t = next(q for q in ge.qubits if q not in (c0, c1))
            if t == a:
                continue

            # require c0, c1, and a all untouched strictly between earlier_idx and compute_idx
            blocked = False
            for k in range(earlier_idx + 1, compute_idx):
                gk = gates[k]
                if c0 in gk.qubits or c1 in gk.qubits or a in gk.qubits:
                    blocked = True
                    break
            if blocked:
                continue

            # require a is untouched (never used) before earlier_idx, so it is still clean |0> there
            a_pre_touched = any(a in gates[k].qubits for k in range(0, earlier_idx))
            if a_pre_touched:
                continue

            # Build rewrite:
            # - everything before earlier_idx unchanged
            # - insert ccx(c0,c1,a) [hoisted compute step] right where the ccz was
            # - replace the ccz itself with cz(a,t)
            # - keep everything between earlier_idx+1 and compute_idx-1 unchanged
            # - drop the original ccx at compute_idx (redundant: a already == c0&c1)
            # - keep everything after compute_idx unchanged
            new_gates = []
            new_gates.extend(gates[:earlier_idx])
            new_gates.append(Gate("ccx", (c0, c1, a)))
            new_gates.append(Gate("cz", (a, t)))
            new_gates.extend(gates[earlier_idx + 1:compute_idx])
            new_gates.extend(gates[compute_idx + 1:])

            new_c = Circuit(c.n, new_gates, c.nc, c.zero_init)
            return new_c, Req(eps=0.0, ancillas=0, measure=True)

    return c, Req()

"""
measured_uncompute_and_reuse_of_parity_ancilla_q9_for_second_cz

Finds a clean AND-ancilla a computed by ccx(c0,c1,a) that is later used only as the
control of cz(a,*) gates and then measured-uncomputed (h a; measure a->cb;
if(cb==1) cz(c0,c1); reset a). If an EARLIER ccz(c0,c1,t) (possibly with c0 and/or c1
X-conjugated, i.e. the actual control polarity differs from the ccx's) exists on the
same control PAIR {c0,c1}, with c0,c1 untouched between that ccz and the ccx compute
step (X gates on c0/c1 are tracked and absorbed as polarity flips, not "touches"),
we hoist the ccx compute step to just before that earlier ccz, turn the ccz into a
free cz(a,t) (inserting an X on a first/after if the polarity differs from the ccx's,
to match a = (c0 XOR p0) & (c1 XOR p1) for the ccz's actual polarity), and delete the
original ccx (now redundant since a already equals the needed parity by then).

Correctness: between the hoisted compute step and the original compute point, c0 and
c1 are only ever acted on by X gates (tracked), so a continues to equal c0&c1 (up to
the X flips, corrected by flipping a) throughout; cz(a,t) with the right polarity of a
reproduces ccz(c0,c1,t) exactly up to that flip, and the existing measured uncompute
at the end still correctly inverts a back to the clean qubit, since the net effect
on (c0,c1,a) of the whole extended segment is identical to the original ccx alone.
Net effect: one Toffoli (7T) is deleted at zero extra cost since the measurement
machinery already existed and is unchanged.
"""
from circuitevolve.circuit import Circuit, Gate
from circuitevolve.verifier import Req


def rewrite(c: Circuit) -> tuple[Circuit, Req]:
    gates = c.gates
    n = len(gates)

    for compute_idx, g in enumerate(gates):
        if g.name != "ccx":
            continue
        c0, c1, a = g.qubits

        # Find the measured-uncompute block for this ancilla a:
        # a used (between compute_idx and h_idx) only as control of cz(a,*),
        # then: h a ; measure a->cb ; if(cb==1) cz(c0,c1) ; reset a
        h_idx = None
        ok = True
        for j in range(compute_idx + 1, n):
            gj = gates[j]
            if a not in gj.qubits:
                continue
            if gj.name == "h" and gj.qubits == (a,):
                h_idx = j
                break
            if gj.name == "cz" and a in gj.qubits:
                continue
            ok = False
            break
        if not ok or h_idx is None:
            continue

        meas_idx = h_idx + 1
        if meas_idx >= n or gates[meas_idx].name != "measure" or gates[meas_idx].qubits != (a,):
            continue
        cbit = gates[meas_idx].cbit

        cond_idx = meas_idx + 1
        if cond_idx >= n:
            continue
        gcond = gates[cond_idx]
        if gcond.name != "cz" or gcond.cond != cbit or set(gcond.qubits) != {c0, c1}:
            continue

        reset_idx = cond_idx + 1
        if reset_idx >= n or gates[reset_idx].name != "reset" or gates[reset_idx].qubits != (a,):
            continue

        # c0, c1 must be untouched (except by X gates, tracked separately) between
        # compute_idx and h_idx, so a stays == parity(c0,c1) throughout.
        touched = False
        for k in range(compute_idx + 1, h_idx):
            gk = gates[k]
            if gk.name == "x" and gk.qubits[0] in (c0, c1):
                continue
            if c0 in gk.qubits or c1 in gk.qubits:
                touched = True
                break
        if touched:
            continue

        # Search earlier (before compute_idx) for a ccz with control-pair exactly {c0, c1},
        # tracking accumulated X-polarity flips on c0/c1 between the candidate and compute_idx.
        pol0 = False  # True = an X on c0 has occurred strictly between candidate ccz and compute_idx
        pol1 = False
        for earlier_idx in range(compute_idx - 1, -1, -1):
            ge = gates[earlier_idx]

            if ge.name == "x" and ge.qubits[0] == c0:
                pol0 = not pol0
                continue
            if ge.name == "x" and ge.qubits[0] == c1:
                pol1 = not pol1
                continue

            if ge.name == "ccz":
                qs = set(ge.qubits)
                if len(qs & {c0, c1}) == 2:
                    t = next(q for q in ge.qubits if q not in (c0, c1))
                    if t == a:
                        continue

                    # require a untouched strictly between earlier_idx and compute_idx
                    a_touched = any(a in gates[k].qubits for k in range(earlier_idx + 1, compute_idx))
                    if a_touched:
                        continue
                    # require a untouched (clean) before earlier_idx too
                    a_pre_touched = any(a in gates[k].qubits for k in range(0, earlier_idx))
                    if a_pre_touched:
                        continue

                    # Build rewrite.
                    new_gates = []
                    new_gates.extend(gates[:earlier_idx])
                    new_gates.append(Gate("ccx", (c0, c1, a)))
                    if pol0:
                        new_gates.append(Gate("x", (a,)))
                        new_gates.append(Gate("cz", (a, t)))
                        new_gates.append(Gate("x", (a,)))
                    elif pol1:
                        new_gates.append(Gate("x", (a,)))
                        new_gates.append(Gate("cz", (a, t)))
                        new_gates.append(Gate("x", (a,)))
                    else:
                        new_gates.append(Gate("cz", (a, t)))
                    new_gates.extend(gates[earlier_idx + 1:compute_idx])
                    new_gates.extend(gates[compute_idx + 1:])

                    new_c = Circuit(c.n, new_gates, c.nc, c.zero_init)
                    return new_c, Req(eps=0.0, ancillas=0, measure=True)
                else:
                    # a ccz not on this control pair but touching c0 or c1 breaks the chain
                    if c0 in qs or c1 in qs:
                        break
                    continue

            # any other gate touching c0 or c1 breaks the chain (polarity tracking
            # only covers plain X gates)
            if c0 in ge.qubits or c1 in ge.qubits:
                break

    return c, Req()

ideas.name: and_tree_for_shared_control_within_toffoli_block
ideas.idea: Each H-conjugated block is a sum of Toffolis x_target ^= sum_k a_k & b_k, i.e. a multiply-controlled XOR of AND terms. Instead of 7 T per AND, compute each AND term into a fresh clean ancilla with a Gidney temporary-AND (measurement-based uncompute, 4 T per AND instead of 7), CX each ancilla into the target, then measured-uncompute all of them. Pattern: a maximal run of ccz(a_k,b_k,t) gates on a common target t, H-conjugated, where no a_k/b_k is touched inside the run. Replace with: for each k, ccx(a_k,b_k,anc_k) realized as a Gidney AND (T-count 4, uses 1 measurement + classically-controlled S/CZ in the uncompute), cz(anc_k,t) -> here just cx(anc_k,t) under the H-conjugation, then H/measure/classically-controlled-CZ uncompute of each anc_k (0 T). This is strictly a different mechanism than phase folding or peephole: it changes the AND to a measured temporary-AND whose uncompute is Clifford, which pyzx/TKET cannot discover because it requires ancillas + mid-circuit measurement. Here there are 25 Toffolis in 9 blocks, so 25*(7-4)=75 T saved. Ancillas can be reused across blocks (one per block-width, max 5), so only ~5 extra qubits and 25 measurements are needed.
ideas.where: All 9 H-conjugated ccz runs: (q10: 4 ccz), (q11: 3), (q12: 2), (q13: 1), (q14: 5), (q13: 4), (q12: 3), (q11: 2), (q10: 1) — 25 Toffolis total.

ideas.name: shared_and_ancilla_across_blocks_for_repeated_control_pairs
ideas.idea: Generalize the existing temporary_and_ancilla rule from 'same control pair twice with the pair untouched between' to 'same control pair appearing anywhere in a region where neither control is ever written'. In this circuit qubits q0..q9 are pure controls: they are NEVER targets of any gate (all cx/ccz targets are q10..q14), so every AND term a&b is valid over the whole circuit. Build one global AND-table: compute each distinct control pair (a,b) into an ancilla once with a Gidney AND (4 T, or 7 T with a plain ccx), use it as a free cz/cx control at every occurrence, and measured-uncompute at the end (0 T). Pattern match: scan for the set of qubits with zero write-events; collect all ccz control pairs drawn from that set; group by pair; for any pair with multiplicity m>=2 emit one AND + m free CZs. Here the pairs are (4,6),(3,7),(2,8),(1,9),(4,7),(3,8),(2,9),(4,8),(3,9),(4,9),(4,5),(3,6),(2,7),(1,8),(0,9),(3,5),(2,6),(1,7),(0,8),(2,5),(1,6),(0,7),(1,5),(0,6),(0,5) — all 25 are DISTINCT, so multiplicity-based fusion alone saves nothing on this instance. The real win is the structural generalization: it makes the control-liveness analysis global (so ancillas can live across the cx layer on q10..q14 and across block boundaries), which is the precondition that lets idea 1 share and batch its ancillas, and it will fire on sibling circuits in this family where pairs repeat. Claimed saving here is only the ancilla-sharing/batching enabled for idea 1, not independent T.
ideas.where: Control register q0..q9 is write-free for the entire circuit; all 25 ccz control pairs qualify. Enables ancilla reuse across the q10..q14 cx mixing layer.

ideas.name: hadamard_conjugated_block_to_phase_polynomial_ancilla
ideas.idea: Each H t ... ccz(a_k,b_k,t) ... H t block is exactly the reversible map t ^= XOR_k (a_k & b_k). Rather than materializing each AND separately, note that the block only needs the single bit s = XOR_k (a_k&b_k) written into t. Pattern: detect an H-conjugated maximal ccz run on target t with all controls write-free; allocate one accumulator ancilla s=|0>; for k=1..n compute a_k&b_k into a scratch ancilla via Gidney AND (4 T each) and cx it into s, uncomputing each scratch immediately (0 T) so only 2 ancillas are needed per block; then cx(s,t); then run the whole accumulation in reverse to clear s (the reverse uses the SAME measured-AND uncompute, 0 T, because the a_k&b_k recomputation can be replaced by replaying the recorded measurement outcomes with classically-controlled Cliffords — no second T cost). Net per block: n ANDs at 4 T = 4n instead of 7n, same as idea 1, but with only 2 extra qubits total (reused across all 9 blocks) instead of up to 5, and the accumulator makes the later cx mixing layer on q10..q14 fold into Clifford corrections that TKET can then clean up. If the measurement-replay trick for the reverse pass does not validate, fall back to idea 1's per-term ancillas; the saving figure below is the incremental benefit over idea 1 (qubit count and Clifford structure), with the T saving already counted there.
ideas.where: All 9 H-conjugated blocks; strongest on the n=5 block (q14: ccz with (4,5),(3,6),(2,7),(1,8),(0,9)) and the two n=4 blocks (q10 first, q13 second).
